Sports.title: The 10 biggest transfers that could still go through on deadline day, including Alvarez to Arsenal and Enzo to Man City
Sports.content:
LET the scramble for last-minute new signings begin!

The Premier League’s top sides could all be active on transfer deadline day today, with the futures of several players still undecided.



Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea, and big-spenders Tottenham are reportedly still in the market to add to their squads.

SunSport looks at the 10 biggest transfers that could STILL happen, starting with the summer’s biggest saga of all.



Julian Alvarez to Arsenal

Will he join or won’t he?

That’s been the question on Arsenal fans’ lips all summer, with the Argentinian being the Premier League champions’ top target in this window.



Of course, he wants Barcelona, but the forward’s club Atletico Madrid don’t want to sell him to their LaLiga rivals.

Reports say that the Gunners are waiting on Alvarez to change his mind and give them the thumbs up and are ready to seal a record British transfer.

However, the fact he is back training with Atletico, following a fan fallout, suggests he might stay put.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Enzo Fernandez to Man City

In what could be a British record £140m transfer fee, Man City are still pursuing Chelsea’s out-of-favour Argentinian Enzo Fernandez.

The midfielder was left out of Xabi Alonso’s squad against Brighton – with the Spaniard tight-lipped about the World Cup winner’s future.

City have finally opened talks with the Blues over reuniting Enzos Fernandez and Maresca.

With Chelsea set to play hard ball, however, this could go right to the wire.

Iliman Ndiaye to Man City

Maresca’s side dramatically hijacked Tottenham’s swoop for Everton star Iliman Ndiaye on Monday.



It is believed Everton had struck an agreement in principle with Spurs for Ndiaye to join for £60million.

But after seemingly missing out on Cody Gakpo, City pivoted to Ndiaye, leaving Spurs’ hopes in tatters.

With Roberto De Zerbi’s side having moved on to Mykhaylo Mudryk, Ndiaye to City feels likely.



Manu Kone, Lamine Camara & Alex Scott to Chelsea

Now, Chelsea are preparing themselves for the departure of Fernandez.

They have contacted several targets to bolster their midfield, including France star Manu Kone.

Transfer expert Fabrizio Romano reports that Chelsea have contacted Kone’s camp to sound out a move from Roma, although there’s been no official bid yet.

Talks with Monaco ace Lamine Camara have reportedly stalled, according to Onze Mondial.

A deal was discussed, but Chelsea have since cooled their interest. But, that could all change.



Alex Scott of Bournemouth looks like a no-goer, though.

The Cherries’ sporting director Thiago Pinto said the playmaker won’t be sold, even though he will enter the final year of his contract in 2027.

Who knows? A monster bid might change that.



Cody Gakpo to Man City or Spurs

Gakpo had looked likely to leave Liverpool all summer, with both Man City and Tottenham heavily linked.

The Dutch winger even agreed personal terms with the former, but Liverpool are reluctant to sanction an £85million deal until they’ve found a replacement.

They completed their huge £123m deal for PSG superstar Bradley Barcola on Monday – but that deal is viewed as separate to Gakpo’s situation.

And, finding someone to fill his shoes in such a short time does look tricky.

Spurs thought they had Gakpo in the bag, until City hijacked their move. Maybe they’ll still have hope, if City switch their attentions to someone else and Liverpool feel the offer is too good to refuse.



Ismaila Sarr or Yankuba Minteh to Liverpool

Which leads us to Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr.

Liverpool see the Senegalese star as the perfect Gakpo replacement, and have reportedly bid around £50million for his services.



That’s not enough for the Eagles, though, who are holding out for £75million, say reports.

The Reds have also had bids for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh rejected too.

The Seagulls want over £60million for the Gambian.



Lewis Hall to Man Utd

Have the Red Devils left a move for Lewis Hall too late?

We won’t know until midnight. But Michael Carrick is said to wanted to sign the player all summer.

Newcastle have insisted the left-back is not for sale, even if United offer an astronomical amount on transfer deadline day.

With Luke Shaw now 31, cover is desperately needed. Will that force United’s hand to send the Toon a huge offer?

Folarin Balogun to Everton

It had appeared that Richarlison was set for a homecoming to the Toffees.



But following an explosive Instagram post on Monday night, it appears that the Brazilian will be remaining at Spurs after all.

Now, in a twist to that saga, Everton are said to have sent a £40m bid to Monaco for former Arsenal striker Folarin Balogun.

With a deal for Richarlison seemingly haven fallen through, Balogun is set to be David Moyes’ new man up top.



Jack Grealish to Everton

Finally, the future of Jack Grealish, the Premier League’s former poster boy, who really needs the Everton move to come through to kick-start his career.

The latest from The Athletic is that Grealish is set for a medical at Everton after the Toffees met City’s demands.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

This would offset the departure of Ndiaye, with Grealish slotting in on the left-side.

Sunderland are also attentive to a potential deal, and could offer the former Aston Villa star a permanent contract – but Everton appear to have won the race.

Sports.title: Arsenal considering deadline day transfer for Lyon’s Malick Fofana with Gunners seeking Martinelli replacement
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are considering a move to sign Lyon winger Malick Fofana.

The Gunners are looking to add attacking reinforcements before Tuesday’s transfer deadline.



Fofana, 21, is on the club’s list of potential additions and transfer chiefs are mulling over making a late move for the Belgian.

Arsenal have already lost Leandro Trossard to Besiktas this summer and are set to sell Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal in a £60m deal too.



The Emirates outfit spent much of their summer pursuing Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior to upgrade their left flank.

But that move was scuppered when the Brazilian penned a new six-year deal to tie him down to the Bernabeu.

Arsenal also explored signing Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa, but the England international ultimately joined Chelsea for £117m.

Fofana represents a market opportunity for Mikel Arteta and Co, who need to add more depth to their left flank.

New signing Christos Tzolis has impressed since his £34m arrival from Club Brugge earlier in the window, but the Greek has little back-up in his position.

Fofana, whose current contract runs until 2028, scored just two goals in 16 games across all competitions for Lyon last season, but has started the new campaign in eye-catching form.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The former Gent ace has already matched his goal tally from last term in only six appearances across Ligue 1 and Champions League qualifying.

Arsenal have also been working on a deal to sign Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid.

However, their chase has hit a stumbling block with the Argentine set on joining Barcelona over the Gunners.

Atletico, however, have no intention of selling their star striker to their fierce Spanish rivals.

Sports.title: ‘I don’t know Jamie Carragher’ – Sunderland ace Wilson Isidor’s blunt response to Sky Sports pundit after relegation tip
Sports.content:
WILSON ISIDOR does not care about Jamie Carragher’s grim Sunderland prediction and claims he has no clue who the Liverpool legend is.

The striker instead vowed to ram the words of any doubters down their throats by proving last season was no “miracle”.



Carragher called Sunderland “arrogant” after the opening day defeat at Ipswich before tipping them for relegation due to the extra demands of the Europa League.

The Black Cats responded with a 1-0 victory over Fulham at the Stadium of Light on Sunday thanks to supersub Isidor’s strike.



Asked to respond to the Sky Sports pundit’s remarks, the spiky Haiti star said: “I don’t know Jamie Carragher. If I don’t know, I don’t have to listen to him.

“People can think about that, but the most important thing that the club showed is they kept the same players who were there last year, and that’s a big, big point from the club that people don’t realise.

“We want to show everybody that last season was not a miracle and Sunderland are really strong and proud to be in the Premier League and also deserve to be in it.

“We want to keep our level like that and to show that the place of Sunderland is in the Premier League and in the upper part of the ranking.”

Isidor only scored six goals during last season’s magical seventh place finish having played second fiddle to Brian Brobbey for the majority of it.

The 26-year-old has been restricted to two cameos off the bench so far this term – but he pleaded with boss Regis Le Bris to unleash him alongside the Dutch powerhouse when they head to Brentford next.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He added: “That’s the… not the dream, but a lot of people want that, and me the first.

“Brian is a different player than me, totally opposite, and the combination of us two can be really amazing.

“That’s the manager’s decision. As I say, he takes his decision, but I would be really happy to play with Brian.

“I just want to score goals. I don’t set a target. I’ve got a good relationship with Brian, so that’s not a bad thing. We know that we have to fight for one spot, but now the gaffer makes the decision.



“Whether it’s me or him, the most important thing for me is to be focused on my performance, on what I can bring on the team, and of course that the team wins.”

One man unlikely to be part of Sunderland’s push this term is winger Jocelin Ta Bi as he closes in on a move to Championship side Burnley.

The 21-year-old, who arrived on Wearside from Israeli side Maccabi Netanya in January, was not included in the squad against Fulham and looks set to switch to Turf Moor on loan.

Sports.title: PSG star earning £150k-a-week turns up to training in £7,000 Peugeot van as fans left stunned
Sports.content:
EVEN a back-to-back Champions League winning midfielder is not above driving around a car worth £7,000.

Yes, Joao Neves has been spotted leaving PSG training in a Peugeot van.



Unless he is a painter and decorator on the side, we can only speculate as to why!

But it wasn’t a brand new van either. It was 2021 Peugeot Partner, available for around £7,000.



Given that Neves is on around £150,000-a-week in the French capital, he probably picked it up with the spare change he had in his pocket!

Most footballers love to flash their expensive cars around the training ground, but clearly Neves is cut from a different cloth.

The TikTok shows the humble star stopping to sign autographs for fans before bolting off in his little van.

Still only 21-years-old, he has been a revelation under Luis Enrique in Paris since his £60million move from Benfica two years ago.

Neves has formed one-half of one of the most formidable midfield partnerships in Europe alongside compatriot Vitinha.

But there has been plenty of change at the club this summer, mostly in the forward line.

Ibrahima Mbaye has left for around £45m to Aston Villa while Bradley Barcola‘s move to Liverpool could end up being worth £123m.

However, both Maghnes Akliouche and Ferran Torres have joined the club in their places.

Sports.title: Robert Sanchez to LEAVE Chelsea just days after Blues signed Emi Martinez as Cesc Fabregas’ Como poach goalkeeper
Sports.content:
ROBERT SANCHEZ is set to leave Chelsea and join Como on loan, according to reports.

The Spaniard was replaced as Blues No1 after Xabi Alonso‘s side signed Emi Martinez from Aston Villa.



And, having immediately lost his spot to the Argentine in the 4-3 win over Brighton on Sunday, Sanchez is now leaving Stamford Bridge.

According to transfer guru Fabrizio Romano, Como have agreed a loan deal with Chelsea to take Sanchez for the season.



The three-cap Spain goalkeeper is likely to replace French stopper Jean Butez as first-choice at Como.

Backup keeper Noel Tornqvist, meanwhile, is set to leave Cesc Fabregas‘ side for Monza.



This is not the first time that Chelsea have done business with Como this summer.

Trevoh Chalobah left the Blues for Fabregas’ side in a £26million deal last month.

With Sanchez gone, Martinez is the undisputed No1 at Chelsea for this season.

The Argentine will be backed up by Mike Penders, who played in the League Cup against Luton last Thursday.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Chelsea could still let several more players leave ahead of the transfer deadline.

Manchester City have finally opened contact regarding a blockbuster move for Enzo Fernandez.

And Tottenham are nearing a double swoop for Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhailo Mudryk.

Adarabioyo is on the brink of a permanent switch to the North Londoners.

Mudryk, meanwhile, is set to reunite with his former Shakhtar Donetsk boss Roberto De Zerbi on loan.

Sports.title: Prem bombshell as UK’s FBI freezes £10m in league’s bank account in unlicensed gambling probe into crypto firm partner
Sports.content:
BRITAIN’S FBI has frozen £10million of Premier League cash as it probes alleged criminality involving a crypto partner fronted by Lionel Messi.

The National Crime Agency is investigating Sorare amid claims of unlicensed gambling.



Sorare, which runs a digital card game backed by Messi and other stars such as Kylian Mbappé, denies any wrongdoing.

The £120million, four-year deal with crypto-gaming firm Sorare was unveiled with a fanfare of publicity in 2023.



But it was terminated at the end of last season as the firm came under investigation in the UK.

We can reveal the National Crime Agency obtained an order from Westminster magistrates’ court in January 2025 freezing £10million under the Proceeds of Crime Act.

It is understood the sum was the first down payment made by Sorare as part of its £30million-a-year deal.

It was held in the Barclays account of the Premier League’s management company.

An NCA spokesperson confirmed the freezing order on funds totalling £10,024,041.33 in the name of The Football Association Premier League Limited.



They added: “The purpose of the order is to prevent dissipation of the funds while the NCA investigates any potential links between those funds and alleged third-party criminality.”

The Premier League is going to court on Monday in a bid to vary the terms of the order, which runs to September 14.

Sorare runs a fantasy sports digital card game, also subject to a prosecution by the Gambling Commission. “Managers” build virtual teams with cards depicting real players. They take part in tournaments with results based on real-world performances.

Announcing the 2023 deal, the Prem said “it will provide fans with another way to connect with their favourite clubs and players”. It gave Sorare rights to release digital cards of players from all 20 teams. In turn, clubs were due to get payments from the Premier League based on player card usage.



The Prem website listed Sorare among its partners. It named investors, ambassadors and advisers to Sorare as Messi — who retired from internationals yesterday — Zinedine Zidane, Kylian Mbappé, Rio Ferdinand, plus tennis star Serena Williams.

The blurb said Sorare was valued at £3.21billion.

Founded in 2018, it was initially a crypto-only marketplace. Users connected wallets and used cryptocurrencies such as Ether or Solana to trade cards.

In August 2023, Sorare officially allowed cash transactions.

Chelsea, City and Spurs in digi deals By Thomas Godfrey CRYPTO dealers have bought their way into football to try to recruit fans as customers. Chelsea last week unveiled Circle as their new front-of-shirt sponsor. It is the first time a crypto company has taken the main shirt slot at a Premier League club, with Joao Pedro among the players to show it off. Crypto exchange OKX has a £55million-a-year deal with Man City, whose stars, including Erling Haaland, wear its logo on their shirt sleeves. Meanwhile, Kraken can be seen on the arm of Pedro Porro and the rest of the Spurs squad. Man United’s training kit was backed by blockchain company Tezos in a deal reportedly worth about £20million a season. The Financial Conduct Authority has recently written to clubs to remind them about fans trusting their badges. FCA director Lucy Castledine said: “They should not let unauthorised financial firms exploit that loyalty by putting potentially dodgy products in front of millions of fans. “A logo on a shirt means one thing — that firm paid for it.”

In 2024, the Gambling Commission launched its prosecution at Birmingham magistrates’ court. It accuses Sorare of providing facilities for gambling without an operating licence. A trial is due next June.



Sorare denies any illegality and says its game is based on skill rather than luck, so should not be subject to betting regulations.

This summer, the Financial Conduct Authority warned football fans were targeted by unauthorised crypto firms and traders obtaining sponsorship deals with clubs.

Sorare said last night: “We cannot comment on the story regarding the freezing order. We would however like to clarify that our contract with the Premier League expired at the end of its term (season 2025-2026).

“As for the Gambling Commission’s prosecution, we firmly deny any claims Sorare is a gambling product under UK laws. The Commission has misunderstood our business and wrongly determined the laws apply to Sorare. We cannot comment further whilst legal proceedings are under way.”

There is no suspicion of any wrongdoing by the Premier League.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It declined to comment about the freezing order.

Latest filed accounts for the year to July 31, 2025, show it has more than £1.5billion. It made charitable donations of £56.6million.

Sports.title: Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1: Bukayo Saka comes to the rescue as uninspiring Gunners maintain 100 per cent start
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA will look to bring in another attacker on deadline day but if his team keep defending like this, he should not have the hump with sporting director Andrea Berta.

Arsenal are once again favourites to retain the title for a very obvious reason.



And it is not because their front three strikes fear into the rest of Europe.

It was their defence, rather than the attack, which was a key reason behind Arsenal winning their first title for 22 years.



After the 3-0 win over Manchester City in the Community Shield and victory by the same scoreline against Coventry, Arsenal bagged another clean sheet here at Villa Park.

Against a typically well-drilled Unai Emery team, who looked much more organised compared to the 4-0 loss to Brighton, Arsenal held firm with Bukayo Saka scoring the winner.



Saka does not score enough goals for a player of his talent, for club or country.

He managed just seven last term but his close-range strike just before the hour doubled his tally for the season.

Ideally, Arsenal will bring in another offensive player, particularly after losing both Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli.

They have spent £164million well. Bruno Guimaraes, who arrived as a second half sub for his Premier League debut, looks certain to improve the midfield.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Defender Ezri Konsa, who enjoyed a decent reception from the home crowd when replacing Cristhian Mosquera in the second half, is also a great arrival.

Christos Tzolis, a £34m signing, enjoyed a bright start for Arsenal both in pre-season and the first couple of games, but looked more like the player who struggled at Norwich and he was substituted at half-time for Eberechi Eze.

Eze, ironically, was substituted at half-time of the 2-1 loss to Villa here last season but he played a part in the winner and he will remain an option out left if Arteta does not get his wish.

As for Aston Villa, they have been unbelievably busy and it will take time for the new signings to make their mark.



There was a debut for Nicolas Jackson who has cost £65million from Chelsea although he has to prove he is an upgrade on Ollie Watkins.

And Villa’s other new arrival who started was keeper Zion Suzuki, a £30m signing from Parma who has replaced Emi Martinez.

He will have to do a bit better at corners than his first effort when he made a complete mess of a Declan Rice set-piece but Gabriel Magalhaes failed to take the chance.



Equally, new signings Alejandro Garnacho and Aaron Wan-Bissaka arrived in the second half as subs but could not help Villa from suffering a second successive defeat although it was not as bad as the opening weekend on the south coast.

Arsenal ratings vs Aston Villa: Saka the game-changer once more as hotheaded Tzolis hooked at half-time BUKAYO SAKA fired Arsenal to a narrow victory over Aston Villa as the Gunners continued their perfect start to the season. Mikel Arteta’s side ground out a close-fought 1-0 victory in a scrappy clash at Villa Park. Neither side ever got close to top hear as it was Saka’s tap-in second-half tap-in was the difference for Arsenal, who are yet to concede a goal this season. There was also a debut for Ezri Konsa, who played just over 10 minutes against his former club following his £51m move earlier in the window. Here’s how SunSport Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall rated the Gunners stars.

This was the first game at Villa Park since Emery’s team won the Europa League final although that does seem an extremely long time ago, particularly after a World Cup and the most bonkers transfer window of all time.

Remarkably, six of the starting XI from that night in Istanbul are no longer at the club in a major revamp which, make no mistake, has been instigated with the full blessing of Emery.

Still, this was hardly a classic.



With Villa Park currently three sides with the North Stand being rebuilt, there were a few builders acting as ballboys behind the goal but they did not have much to do.

Emi Buendia, who scored the 95th minute winner last December, saw a shot smash against the bar.

Had that shot gone in there would have been uproar, unless VAR would have intervened, as Boubacar Kamara did seem to foul Tzolis.



For the second half, it was not a huge surprise that Arteta acted with Eze coming on and in their first attack, helped by Ross Barkley initially giving the ball away, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty.

Yet while Ian Maatsen’s clumsy challenge on Saka was definitely a free-kick, VAR spotted that it happened just outside the area while Martin Odegaard’s free-kick was poor.

Yet Villa refused to heed the warning and they were undone by a decent move by Arsenal although Victor Lindelof could have done better by blocking the cross from Riccardo Calafiori.



Mosquera started the move with a fantastic pass to Eze and once Calafiori delivered the cross, Saka was in a perfect position to beat Maatsen to the ball.

Villa pushed for an equaliser but Arsenal’s defence held strong in the eight minutes of stoppage time.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

At last week’s PFA awards, the Premier League team of the season included Arsenal keeper David Raya and three of his defenders.

There is an obvious reason for that and it looks as though they will be equally as mean this season.

Sports.title: Saka earns hard-fought win for Arsenal at Villa
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka's goal just before the hour mark was enough for champions Arsenal to maintain their perfect start with a 1-0 win over Aston Villa at Villa Park.

This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka breaks the deadlock

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emi Buendia's 20-yard effort smashes the bar – but was there a foul just before?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player VAR overturns an Arsenal penalty as contact is ruled to be outside the box

Arsenal's talisman thought he had won a penalty early in the second half but Ian Maatsen's foul was ruled to be outside the box following a VAR review. It mattered not because he forced in Riccardo Calafiori's centre from close range soon afterwards.

The home side, who included debutants Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson in their starting line-up, pushed for an equaliser but Arsenal, who brought on former Villa man Ezri Konsa late on, stayed strong to claim the win. A show of strength by the champions.

Still no shot on target for Villa Aston Villa are not only without a point from their opening two games but they are yet to register a shot on target.

The key moments from Villa Park

12 - BAR! Buendia lashes the ball against Raya's crossbar

56 - VAR! Saka denied penalty as Maatsen's foul is outside box

59 - GOAL! Calafiori's low cross is forced into the net by Saka

75 - MISS! Suzuki saves one-on-one from Havertz but he is off

Arteta hails 'massive win'

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta speaking to Sky Sports:

"Really happy. A massive win. A tough place to come and earn the three points. We deserved it. A great squad performance - because when 11 wasn't enough the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to finish off the game.

"Last year we lost here in a really difficult way, with the last kick of the game. And that was still in the tummy.

"We are in the second game and it's like, 'we have to win this game!'

"We know that last year was the same. We know the level, we know how difficult it is for every team to earn points in this league, so we have to be really proud tonight."

Emery focuses on the positives

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports:

"We've lost. We competed well. We are trying to rebuild the team but a lot of positive things after the result. How we compete defensively, with the ball. We didn't create clear chances but we didn't concede clear chances. It was so equal, the match.

"Some players made their debut, fantastic. Suzuki, Jackson both very good work. The first step forward, Today is positive for the next matches.

"To lose one match is painful but after we must try to get positive things. This is the reason I am being optimistic. There are 38 matches, we played two matches and didn't achieve points but hopefully we can get better."

Arsenal's depth stands out

Tzolis has made a promising start to his Arsenal career but this was a more difficult evening for him. The response from Arteta? Bring on Eze. He helped open it up for Arsenal to win. When Villa pushed, the Arsenal boss turned to Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino to battle it out.

"Guimaraes demonstrated already with a couple of passes he's going to be something very different to what they've already got," said Gary Neville on co-commentary for Sky Sports.

"He cuts through with his passing; he always looks for that furthest forward pass. Arsenal sometimes are guilty of recycling it too much - he won't do that."

But just as significant was how robust Arsenal looked in seeing this out. As well as the physical midfield trio, Konsa came on for Cristhian Mosquera. Villa did not even manage a shot on target. Rock solid.

With different players for different situations and back-to-back wins, the Gunners have already shown why they are still the team to beat in the Premier League. And they might just have got better.

Suzuki impresses on debut

As Premier League debuts go, replacing World Cup-winning goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez for a game against the champions Arsenal right in front of the Holte End must be among the more daunting. Suzuki acquitted himself impressively for Aston Villa.

The Japan goalkeeper failed to claim one early cross but when he tipped over a near-post header soon after, the Villa fans were chanting 'the world's number one' - a playful reference to the popular chant that was traditionally directed at Martinez at Villa Park.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville hails Ederson-esque pass from Zion Suzuki for Aston Villa

There was a little more lustre to the chant later in the first half when Suzuki pinged a pass out to George Hemmings on the left wing - arrowing the ball with extraordinary power. His distribution with both feet already looks likely to be a weapon for the team.

Suzuki did spill one fiercely struck shot in the second half but he denied Kai Havertz when one-on-one - not knowing that the offside flag would go up. Even in defeat, it was an encouraging showing by the new Villa goalkeeper.

Sports.title: Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Sabalenka also wins
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open.

Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.

The severity of the injury, which did not require surgery, meant Alcaraz was a doubt for the US Open but he entered Flushing Meadows and showed with his 6-4 6-4 6-4 win over Safiullin that he cannot be dismissed from defending his title from last year.

Henman: Alcaraz got the game he wanted Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman



"If you’d have asked Alcaraz how he’d have liked this game to go, he would have signed up for a straight-sets victory, a few pressure moments, and just over two hours work.



"That is exactly what he got today. He and his team will be delighted with all aspects of this game."

"There were some doubts in the match, I'm not going to lie. Thinking about if I would last the match, best of five, playing four or five sets," said Alcaraz, who will play Portugal's Jaime Faria in the next round.

"I had a little bit of doubt, but I tried to forget everything and focus on the things I needed to improve. I thought about what would happen in the match and physically I felt really well."

Watched on by rapper Travis Scott, who helped design Alcaraz's brown outfit for the US Open, there was plenty of attention on the seven-time Grand Slam champion's serve and groundstroke speed, given he had not played competitive singles for over four months.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz reflected on his US Open round one win. against Roman Safiullin

He needed to save two break points from Safiullin in his opening three service games before breaking himself in the eighth game which proved enough to claim the opening set.

Alcaraz was broken at the start of the second set but broke back immediately and upped his intensity to break in the eighth game again and go on to win the second set.

After an early break in the third set, Alcaraz never came under threat on his serve and continued to move well while maintaining a high level on both wins to see off the tricky Russian.

One of the biggest threats in Alcaraz's half was Arthur Fils, after he won the Cincinnati Open title last week, but he was knocked out of the tournament by Stefanos Tsitsipas in a 4-6 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 6-4 defeat.

Sabalenka overcomes Osorio test

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Aryna Sabalenka and Camila Osorio

Like Alcaraz, Aryna Sabalenka started her US Open title with a straight-sets win as she beat Colombia's Camila Osorio 6-2 6-4.

Sabalenka is bidding to become the first player to win three consecutive US Open titles since Serena Williams in 2014 and was put under serious pressure by Osorio in the second set.

"Camila is a tough opponent but I was ready to do whatever it takes to get the win," she told Sky Sports Tennis.

"I really enjoyed the atmosphere and support. A fun and tough match but happy to get through in straight sets."

Sabalenka's form has been questioned after losing in the last 16 in her last three tournaments - Wimbledon, the Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open.

It means she could lose her status as world No 1 for the first time since October 2024 with Elena Rybakina, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula all having the chance to knock Sabalenka off her perch.

But Sabalenka's best surface is the hard court, having won her four Grand Slam titles on hard, and her raw power will always make the Belarusian difficult to beat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka hits back at critics, saying she is tired of the negativity surrounding her with everything she does both on and off the court

Elsewhere, Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova will be looking for another big run and she got off to a great start by beating Austria's Sinja Karus 6-3 6-0.

Last year's US Open runner-up Amanda Anisimova defeated compatriot Ashlyn Krueger 6-1 6-3 and was joined by three more victorious Americans in the women's draw on Monday as Emma Navarro, Taylor Townsend and Cate McNally also won.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How many previous US Open winners could you name in 20 seconds?

Brits Dart and Fearnley fight back to progress; Wendelken out

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Jacob Fearnley and Martin Landaluce

Britain's Harriet Dart and Jacob Fearnley both fought back from losing positions to reach the second round of the US Open.

Dart was a set and a break down before roaring back to a 3-6 6-3 6-2 win over American Peyton Stearns.

Her coach and Sky Sports Tennis pundit Marion Bartoli said: "I'm really pleased for her. Such a great effort and mentally it's so hard to come back but she fought so hard. It's absolutely brilliant."

That was followed by a superb win for Jacob Fearnley after he beat Spain's Martin Landaluce 4-6 6-2 4-6 7-5 6-3.

Landaluce served for the match in the fourth set but Fearnley won three games in a row to take the match to a deciding set and continued that momentum in the fifth.

Despite missing a routine smash to win the match, Fearnley kept his composure and ensured he made the second round at Flushing Meadows for a second successive year.

Sports.content:

Sabalenka is attempting to regain her usual dominance after a frustrating last six months, ​having failed to reach a final since she completed the Sunshine Double in March, but she made a confident start to her quest for a ‌rare 'three-peat' at the year's final major.

Sports.title: McIlroy: 'Grumpy' world No 2 needs 'new goal' after FedEx Cup claims
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy needs to assess how much he truly wants to be world No 1 again alongside balancing his home life, according to former golfer Rob Lee.

The Northern Irishman finished in a seven-way tie for fourth at the FedEx Cup over the weekend, finishing five shots off tournament winner Scottie Scheffler despite showing earlier signs of promise.

Now 37, six-time major winner McIlroy admitted his "fuse was shorter than it used to be" before the final round at the East Lake Golf Club.

Image: Rory McIlroy has admitted his patience with the demands of professional golf is thinning

He had arrived in Atlanta off the back of three weeks of competing in a row, something he admitted he would never exceed again despite still managing a fourth-place finish over the weekend.

"That just tells you how good he is," Lee told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast. "But I think Rory's body language this week wasn't great. He looked slightly… is grumpy the right word?

"But he's just slightly off that kind of affable, bouncy Rory that we normally see. So there's stuff going on with him… Rory's in this position. He's played golf for 20 years at the highest level. He's 37.

"He realises there are other things in life, but the last thing he wants to do is not be able to be peak Rory. So his conundrum is 'how much can I pare back my schedule, but still perform the way I know I can?' That's the place he's in now.

"37 is still golfing prime. It's going to come down, for him, to desire. How much does he still want it? And if he still wants it, I think he's going to have to play a bit more."

McIlroy took an extended break after The Open, spending more time with his family before returning for this three-week run of events.

Image: Scheffler clinched his second FedExCup title after he secured a three-shot victory at the Tour Championship

"I absolutely think he can win more majors," Lee continued. "But going along with that is you sacrifice your home life. You're not as home as much as you want to be… I actually think Rory is in mentally quite a good place at the moment, and he is focused on some family stuff at the moment."

Speaking before his final round, McIlroy admitted: "once you lose your enthusiasm to go to the course, it is time to take a break." That comment could suggest golf fans could be seeing less and less of the world No 2 as time goes on.

"I think that's plausible," Sean Zak agreed. "I think that the changes coming to the PGA Tour schedule could pull a little bit more out of him, could help him balance being a dual member a little bit better."

Zak went on to suggest McIlroy may need to set himself a goal of beating Scheffler to top spot to reignite his motivation.

"You know, of all the golfers at the top of the game, I think he better than most shows what things matter to him and shows the goals that he's set," he said.

"And I think ever since that Grand Slam-finishing Masters win, he has just struggled to really place "OK, what's the next goal?"

Image: Rory McIlroy won the Masters in 2025 and 2026

"When you look at 2025, when he won that Masters, the next goal was really, 'OK, let's win at Bethpage' - and then they did that.

"Then after that, it was 'gosh, OK, what is the next goal?' I think for him to live up to what we're asking him to do right now, what a lot of fans would like him to do, is his next goal needs to be taking Scottie off the top mark or matching Scottie in some way.

"I bet if Scottie won a major this year, Rory might feel a little bit more of the fire beneath him because you get to some point where they've all won a bunch.

"What is the tiebreaker? How many majors did you win? Rory still has a nice little lead on Scottie - but how long will that last? We think that he probably won't hold that lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sean Zak from golf.com asks what is Rory McIlroy's next goal after his grand slam Masters win?

"It's just funny because I think Rory McIlroy, let's say [at] 21 years old was like "I want to be number one in the world. I want to win every single tournament."

"Rory McIlroy, 37-year-old, he may have to do the same thing. It should be 'I want to be number one. I want the world to think I'm the best golfer because at my best, I certainly am.'"

McIlroy will next compete at the Irish Open, starting on September 10.

Sports.title: Man City agree £65m Ndiaye deal as Spurs turn attention to Mudryk
Sports.content:
Manchester City have agreed a £65m deal with Everton for winger Iliman Ndiaye as an alternative to Cody Gakpo.

With contact already established between City and Everton over Jack Grealish, discussions have moved swiftly.

City's deal is broken up into a £60m guaranteed payment plus £5m in bonuses.

Richarlison's reluctance to make a final decision on a move to Everton held up Spurs' advanced talks involving Ndiaye that had been ongoing since yesterday.

It means Tottenham are looking to alternative targets and have started talks with Chelsea about a loan for Mykhailo Mudryk.

Earlier on Monday, Liverpool rejected City's £80m bid for Cody Gakpo.

Sky Sports News understands Liverpool are concerned about their chances of bringing in a replacement for the Dutchman.

Manchester City want to sign a wide forward and a central midfielder before the window closes.

City also opened talks with Chelsea for Enzo Fernandez on Monday.

Manchester City allowed Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham earlier month, reducing Enzo Maresca's options on the wing.

City did not name a winger on their bench in Friday's win over Crystal Palace and started with Phil Foden - who Enzo Maresca admitted is not a winger - out wide at Selhurst Park.

Liverpool signed Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday while Victor Munoz arrived from Osasuna earlier this summer.

Spurs also targeted Gakpo in this window before signing Savio and Marmoush.

Sports.title: Saka settles gruelling battle with Aston Villa to extend Arsenal’s winning start
Sports.content:
The smile on Declan Rice’s face with six minutes of normal time remaining said it all. He had just shut down Ian Maatsen as the Aston Villa full-back zoomed into the box. Arsenal, for whom Bukayo Saka scored the only goal, were authoritative and seemingly took great satisfaction in keeping Villa at arm’s length.

Unai Emery’s work‑in‑progress side struggled to test the champions, David Raya untroubled. The records will show Villa have lost their first two league matches of a season without scoring for the first time since 2002 but, despite successive defeats, this time there was no capitulation.

For Villa, this was a marked improvement on defeat at Brighton in their opener. After 31 minutes in their previous game, they trailed 4-0 and after 40 were down to 10 men.

Here they could take plenty of encouragement from a promising if not fruitless performance, the debutants Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson impressing, having taken the No 1 and No 11 shirts vacated by Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins respectively. Suzuki and Jackson were the only changes to Villa’s starting XI but they appeared far more cohesive. Suzuki’s eye for a pass was particularly noticeable, pinging 50-yard passes to George Hemmings, the 19-year-old who kept his place, and John McGinn within a few minutes of each other.

Emi Buendía smacked the crossbar after Boubacar Kamara overawed Christos Tzolis – Martin Ødegaard subsequently asked questions of the referee, Jarred Gillett – but Jackson otherwise created Villa’s best opening. The Senegal forward, who worked under Emery at Villarreal, pinched possession from Gabriel Magalhães a few yards into the Villa half and galloped into the other before sending a near-perfect cross in from the right. Hemmings burst into the six-yard box but was unable to convert. Villa are just the second team to fail to register a shot on target in their first two Premier League matches in a season since 2003-04, along with Swansea City in 2017-18.

This fixture last season ended in despair for Arsenal, their players splayed across the turf after Buendía’s 95th-minute winner with the last kick of the game. Arteta said that defeat still haunts him and reminded his players as much before this game. “That was still in my tummy and I spoke to my players about it, the image of the players on the floor, totally gutted,” the Arsenal manager said. “We used that [as inspiration].”

View image in fullscreen Zion Suzuki, Aston Villa’s new goalkeeper, applauds the home fans after the final whistle. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

In that game last season Eberechi Eze was at fault for Matty Cash’s opener and was subsequently hooked at half-time. Here it was a case of role‑reversal, Eze shining after coming on for the second half in place of Christos Tzolis, who was booked after a foul on Cash and muted.

“I think he learnt a lesson,” Arteta said of Eze, who was involved in Arsenal seizing the lead approaching the hour. Arsenal slowed things down and then punished Villa for switching off. Cristhian Mosquera pushed a pass to Eze, who was afforded space by Cash, Villa’s defender concerned about an unmarked Riccardo Calafiori. Eze promptly spied Calafiori’s underlapping run and the Italian steered the ball across the six-yard box where Saka beat Maatsen to the punch and scrambled the cross into the net.

This is a new-look Villa, on and off the pitch. A handful of staff in hard hats were positioned in the closed North Stand moonlighting as ball boys; the corner of rubble between the remaining skeleton and the Trinity Road Stand remains akin to an excavation site. Ibrahim Mbaye, whose £47m move from Paris Saint‑Germain is to be announced on Tuesday, was in the directors’ box. Taylor Harwood-Bellis is also poised to sign in a £25m deal from Southampton. Six of Villa’s starting XI from their Europa League triumph may have departed but Emery has made no complaints and has relayed his no-excuses mantra to his squad. “We do not look backwards,” he said.

Villa’s frustrations were palpable. McGinn, in a hurry to get Villa level, was booked for wiping out Merino. Aaron Wan-Bissaka replaced Cash for his Villa debut and his first job was to stretch his legs to muffle an advancing Eze. Alejandro Garnacho entered in place of Ross Barkley. Arteta introduced Ezri Konsa for his debut, adding further steel.

Villa could not find a way through and Arsenal’s winning habit already appears ominous. “It is painful to lose,” Emery said. “But we can feel optimistic with how we competed.”

Sports.title: Argentina’s Lionel Messi retires from international football: ‘This hurts me a lot’
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football seven weeks after Argentina were beaten by Spain in the World Cup final in the US. The 39-year-old captained Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022 and two Copa América titles after winning his first cap in 2005.

On Monday, Messi posted a picture on Instagram of notes that he wrote on 21 July, two days after the World Cup final, confirming he was ending his Argentina career and said the death of his father, Jorge, in early August made him feel “more convinced than before”. Messi was often visibly emotional during the tournament and revealed in the knockout stages that Jorge was undergoing medical treatment.

Messi’s statement, addressed to Argentina fans, read: “After the time that has passed since the final, thinking a lot, I want to let everyone know that I am retiring from the national team. It is a decision that hurts my soul but I know it is time. I can say for sure that I always gave everything, not only in the last few years when we won everything [but] before as well, and I always fought and gave everything for the shirt, to give you joy and make you proud of being Argentinian through football.

“There’s not long left and chapters are coming to an end – and this is one that hurts me a lot. I love, have loved and I will always love being part of the national team. I have emptied myself: now I have nothing more to give and, besides, there are great young players coming through who deserve to be [selected].”

Messi thanked his family for accompanying him on a “beautiful but difficult journey”. He previously announced his retirement from international football in 2016 after Argentina lost on penalties to Chile in the 2016 Copa América final – at the time his fourth defeat in a major final out of four. The then Barcelona forward was often criticised for not producing his club form at international level and comparisons were constantly made with the World Cup-winning Diego Maradona. However, Messi was persuaded to continue and finally lifted silverware with his country at the 2021 Copa América in Brazil.

“I take with me unforgettable memories and moments,” his statement said. After victory against Brazil at the Maracanã in the 2021 Copa América final, Messi was central to Argentina’s first World Cup triumph since 1986 and scored in every knockout round in Qatar, including twice in the final against France – two years after the death of Maradona.

Quick Guide How do I 

Argentina defended their Copa América title in 2024 amid speculation that Messi, by then playing for Inter Miami, would call it a day. He turned 39 during the World Cup this summer, briefly becoming the tournament’s all-time record scorer before being overtaken by Kylian Mbappé.

His statement finished by returning to address Argentina fans: “I go with the satisfaction and the pride of having, along with my teammates, giving you moments we dreamed about. I love you! I thank God for making me Argentinian.”

Messi retires as Argentina’s record appearance maker – he won the first of his 207 caps in a friendly against Hungary in August 2005 and was sent off almost immediately for catching Vilmos Vanczak with an elbow. He is also Argentina’s record scorer with 125 goals. Before playing for the senior team, he won the Under-20 World Cup and also won Olympic gold in 2008.

Since the end of his sixth World Cup, Messi has featured seven times for Inter Miami and scored four goals in the 7-1 rout of Montreal in Major League Soccer on Saturday. Messi signed a contract extension last year to 2028, when he will be 41.

Ángel Di María, who scored for Argentina in the 2021 Copa América and 2022 World Cup finals, led tributes from Messi’s former teammates, writing: “All I know is that I was born in the right century to be able to see you, enjoy you and, above all, share with you all these years [together] with the national team.” The midfielder Rodrigo de Paul posted: “Thank you for making us so happy. You can’t imagine how many times you made people smile. You are eternal.”

As a teenager, Enzo Fernández wrote to Messi to plead with him to reverse his 2016 decision to retire from Argentina duty, trying to work out if he would be old enough to play alongside him one day. “That kid was so lucky … Thank you for letting me share a part of your story,” Fernández said. “We’re going to miss you so much, capitán,” said the striker Lautaro Martínez.

Sports.title: Manchester City gazump Spurs over Iliman Ndiaye and eye Enzo Fernández deal
Sports.content:
Manchester City are poised to bolster their attack by buying Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye for up to £65m and have opened talks with Chelsea over a deal to sign Enzo Fernández.

City’s hijack of Tottenham’s deal for Ndiaye came after their attempts to sign Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo broke down. The Senegal international is poised to undergo a medical after a fee of £60m plus £5m in add-ons was agreed with Everton, who have little time to find a replacement for one of their most important players before the transfer window shuts on Tuesday night.

It had seemed that Ndiaye would move to Spurs after they agreed a deal in principle with Everton on Sunday. Richarlison was poised to move in the opposite direction but that transfer stalled on Monday. Richarlison released an emotional statement on social media and said that he would not allow his future to be decided for him. The Brazilian is cool on a move to Everton and is expected to stay at Spurs.

City registered their interest in Ndiaye last week and moved in after Liverpool pulled out of an £85m deal for Gakpo. Spurs have moved on and agreed to sign Mykhailo Mudryk on loan from Chelsea.

The Ukraine winger, who is free to play again after his doping ban was resolved this summer, played for Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk and favoured a reunion with the Tottenham manager after Leeds and Brentford also contacted Chelsea about him.

Spurs have also agreed a deal to sign Chelsea’s defender Tosin Adarabioyo on a permanent deal.

Chelsea are poised for a busy end to the window and have finally been contacted by City about Fernández. The Argentina midfielder wants to leave and has his heart set on a move to City. Fernández has a close relationship with City’s manager, Enzo Maresca, who left Chelsea this year.

Chelsea set a price of £120m for Fernández this summer and may push for a higher fee with the deadline drawing close. Another consideration for the Stamford Bridge club as they face up to losing one of their biggest players is the need to improve their squad.

Chelsea have sounded out Roma’s Manu Koné and Monaco’s Lamine Camara as potential replacements for Fernández. They have been met with resistance in attempts to sign Bournemouth’s Alex Scott while Crystal Palace want to keep Adam Wharton. Chelsea are tracking Morgan Gibbs‑White but know Nottingham Forest are unlikely to sell at this stage.

The goalkeeper Robert Sánchez is poised to leave Chelsea as he nears a loan to Como. Sánchez lost the No 1 spot after Emiliano Martínez’s arrival.

Sports.title: Arsenal trying to lure Julián Álvarez after agreeing deals to sell Martinelli and Jesus
Sports.content:
Arsenal are running out of time to persuade Julián Álvarez to join them from Atlético Madrid after agreeing to sell Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fábio Vieira in deals collectively worth more than £70m.

Álvarez has his heart set on joining Barcelona despite Atlético’s insistence they will not sell to their La Liga rivals – he returned to training on Sunday after being left out of their squad for the win against Sevilla.

Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, is understood to have spoken last week to Álvarez in an effort to persuade the former Manchester City forward to return to the Premier League and to have been informed the Argentina international wants only Barcelona.

Asked directly about Álvarez after victory at Aston Villa on Monday, Arteta replied: “I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.”

But Arsenal’s manager did confirm they are seeking reinforcements. “We are trying to improve the squad and until tomorrow night we are going to do that,” he said. “I have been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now.”

Barcelona have agreed an £8.6m deal to sign Jesus, who has entered the final year of his contract after falling down the pecking order behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres. The 29-year-old Brazilian was at Camp Nou to watch the 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday. The Barcelona manager, Hansi Flick, said: “He’s a top striker and of course for us very important, he can give us a lot of things and [I’m] very happy that he’s here.”

However, the Spanish champions would like to sign another attacker after selling Ferran Torres to Paris Saint-Germain and are said to have not given up on Álvarez.

Atlético have agreed a deal with Juventus for Jonathan David on an initial loan with an option to make the Canada forward’s move permanent next summer. But they are understood to be determined to keep Álvarez, who joined from City in 2024.

Arsenal remain hopeful that the 26‑year‑old could change his mind but are believed to be monitoring several other attacking options. Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye was among the players on their shortlist but Manchester City are in advanced talks over a £65m deal for the Senegal forward. Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea and failed in an ambitious attempt to sign Vinícius Júnior, the Brazil forward signing a contract extension at Real Madrid.

Arsenal have signed Christos Tzolis to replace Leandro Trossard on the left but Martinelli’s expected departure to Al-Hilal for a club‑record £56m sale would create a space in the squad, although Eberechi Eze is also capable of playing there.

Martinelli, who scored six times in the Champions League last season but only once in the Premier League, was due to have his medical on Monday after being left out of Arsenal’s squad against Coventry on the opening weekend. His fee surpasses the £40m Liverpool paid Arsenal for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.

Vieira looks poised to join Hamburg, where he was on loan last season, for £8.6m.

Sports.title: Liverpool sign Barcola in £123m deal and expect Gakpo to stay after City offer £80m
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola is aiming to win the Premier League after completing his move to Liverpool from Paris Saint‑Germain for an initial £106m, which could rise to £123m. The France international has signed a five-year deal.

Andoni Iraola has prioritised signing wingers this summer after replacing Arne Slot. Barcola follows the arrival of Victor Muñoz as the former Bournemouth head coach aims to rebuild the front line.

“It took a long time but I’m really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play,” Barcola said. “I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it’s one of my biggest dreams in my life. It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that’s why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.”

Barcola, who will be 24 on Wednesday, was a long-term target for Liverpool, who have tracked his progress over a number of seasons. Completing the transfer has been delayed while PSG waited to make signings to compensate for the exit of the former Lyon player, who attracted interested from other clubs but was adamant that he was willing to join only Liverpool.

Quick Guide How do I 

“When I knew about Liverpool’s interest in me, I didn’t ask questions and I knew it was a very big club for me,” Barcola said.

The Frenchman will probably be Liverpool’s final incoming. The club are expecting Cody Gakpo to stay after rejecting an £80m offer from Manchester City for the Dutchman over the weekend. Liverpool would regard selling a first-team player at this stage as problematic because it would allow little time to source a replacement.

Harvey Elliott is expected to join Valencia on loan for the season. The midfielder returned this summer from a similar spell at Aston Villa, where he failed to make an impression and although he was part of the pre-season plans, has failed to make the squad for the opening two Premier League fixtures.

Liverpool have targeted younger players in this window, evidenced by the signings of Barcola, the 21‑year‑old Jérémy Jacquet and the 23‑year‑old Muñoz in the hope of building a squad for the long term.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 11: Manchester City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 1st (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st

Prospects

Champions again at last, after a 10-year wait, Manchester City now face an even tougher task: defending their title. They appear to have a good chance of succeeding, especially after keeping their star striker, Khadija “Bunny” Shaw. The WSL’s top scorer and best player of 2025-26 performed a dramatic U-turn by signing a new four-year contract in May rather than leaving on a free transfer, and that may prove crucial in continuing City’s positive momentum.

Their squad looks to be of a similar strength to last season. The Brazil forward Kerolin left for Barcelona but Beth Mead arriving from Arsenal in essence replaces her. Similarly, the exit of left-back Leila Ouahabi will be compensated for by the acquisition of Niamh Charles from Chelsea. Perhaps the only minor question is whether there is sufficient depth to sustain a challenge in the Women’s Champions League as well as domestically, but the core of regulars looks as formidable as any club in Europe.

The team scored plenty last term and had great success down the flanks, with the right-back Kerstin Casparij providing the joint-most assists in the division. Defensively they look solid. The most intriguing challenge could be psychological, as they switch from hunters to hunted, becoming the team that everybody wants to beat. They start at home to one of the promoted sides, Birmingham City, and first meet a fellow title hopeful – Arsenal – at the start of October, when they will aim to lay down a marker in the title race.

Off-field picture

Owned by City Football Group and led off the pitch by the managing director, Charlotte O’Neill, and director of football, Therese Sjögren, City enter the season with a new women’s team building at the training centre. The £10m building offers everything from underwater treadmills to a barista-style coffee machine in the canteen, with every element tailored towards maximising performance for female athletes. Previously the women’s team sometimes had to share a gym with City’s boys’ academy.

The manager

Andrée Jeglertz’s first season could scarcely have gone better, as he oversaw a league and cup double. He arrived in Manchester after a relatively uninspiring spell in charge of Denmark women but his CV is full of extensive high-level experience, including a 2004 European title with the Swedish club Umeå. The 54-year-old is a calm presence on the touchline, unwavering in his belief that his team will “find a way to win”, and has avoided controversy in press conferences, which he handles assuredly.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Beth Mead joins the champions from rivals Arsenal. Photograph: Kate Green/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

Mead was the headline signing on a free transfer after nine years at Arsenal. City are hoping that the England forward – the Golden Boot winner and player of the tournament at the 2022 European Championship – is not past her best, at 31, and can flourish across a three-year contract. She is the all-time leading assist provider in the WSL. Mead also has 81 caps and will want to be part of any Lionesses squad at next summer’s World Cup.

Stat attack

If teams want to defend more effectively against the champions, they could start by focusing on free-kicks and corners. City scored at least twice as many set-piece goals as anyone else in 2025-26. As strong as they were elsewhere, this was their superpower.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Set for a breakthrough

The 18-year-old full-back Sacha Lewis signed her first professional contract with City in August, having been with the club since under-14 level. The younger sister of the club’s men’s first-team full-back Rico Lewis, she has been a regular for England Under-19s and has been named in the England Under-20 squad that will go to Poland for September’s Women’s Under-20 World Cup. She was the player of the season for Manchester City’s “Next Gen” team last term and, with City juggling European and domestic football, may get a chance in the first team.

What they say

“Our biggest challenge this year is to continue winning and, at the same, compete in other competitions and also want to win those. Winning in one year is one thing, but being able to win in the next year, that is even tougher. Of course we can do that [compete on multiple fronts] and we have good enough players to be able to play with one starting XI on Saturday and do a couple of changes on Wednesday and still win. That was our biggest challenge last year – we had too many good players that were not playing enough games, so this year we will have the possibility to explore the whole squad. Each player will be more important than they’ve ever been for the club” – Jeglertz speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live.

Where are they playing their home games?

The Joie Stadium is the women’s team’s usual home, across the road from the Etihad Stadium, where they will play two home league fixtures. Those will be against Arsenal on 4 October and against Manchester United on 14 February. The 7,000-capacity Joie Stadium, that hosted matches at Euro 2022, has been the women’s team’s home for more than a decade and they were unbeaten at home in the league last season. They haven’t lost a home WSL game at the Joie Stadiumsince a 4-3 thriller against Arsenal in February 2025.

Sports.title: Fifa extends ban on man who secretly filmed female footballers in Austria
Sports.content:
Fifa has extended worldwide the ban on a former match official and SCR Altach employee found guilty of taking secret videos and photographs of members of the club’s women’s team.

In February, a regional court in Feldkirch, Austria, handed the man a seven-month suspended prison sentence, a €1,200 (£1,046) fine and ordered him to pay the victims €625 (£545) each in compensation after he was found guilty of filming and taking photographs of players, including minors, in the changing room, gym and showers of Altach’s women’s team between 2018 and 2025.

The sentence provoked outrage from former Altach players and more widely in Austria. After a request from the Austrian players’ union (VdF) and the global players’ union Fifpro, the Fifa disciplinary committee extended on 4 August the man’s ban from football-related activities to a global one. A Fifa spokesperson said: “In line with article 70 of the Fifa disciplinary code, the Fifa disciplinary committee has extended the sanction imposed on an official by the Austrian FA to have worldwide effect.”

Quick Guide How do I 

The man did not request a statement of the reasons for the decision within a prescribed timeframe, so the decision has become binding and final. Federations are able to ban individuals from football related activities only in their respective countries.

Christos Papadimitriou, the women’s football coordinator at the VdF, said: “Anyone who secretly films players in the locker room crosses a clear line. The fact that the ban now applies worldwide sends an important signal: those who seriously violate players’ rights cannot escape the consequences by moving abroad.”

The Czech players’ union, CAFH, has called for a lifetime ban from all football-related activities for Petr Vlachovsky, the former coach of FC Slovacko, who was convicted of similar offences in addition to being in possession of child sexual abuse material. Vlachovsky was convicted in May 2025 and handed a suspended one-year prison sentence and five-year domestic coaching ban.

In March Fifpro said: “Because the Czech criminal process and the Czech FA’s administrative proceedings are separate and can run in parallel, the union is challenging the FA to implement a lifetime football ban for Vlachovsky and all sexual offenders. Fifpro is exploring possible legal avenues on behalf of players to achieve a global ban.”

Sports.title: Chelsea’s perfect yet unserious start to the Premier League season | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Two Premier League games played for Chelsea under Xabi Alonso: two wins and seven goals scored. It’s the sort of start that would delight many new managers – only two other clubs can boast about a six-point start this Premier League season (albeit with Arsenal to play later on Monday). Points gained in this odd transitional phase, when almost nobody seems quite ready, could prove extremely valuable come the end of the season. And yet, for all the attacking potency, there must also be concerns about Chelsea’s openness and the five goals conceded.

Context must also be considered, and it projects both ways. It’s early in the season. There has been, as ever, a lot of change at Chelsea. They will get better; they will achieve greater coherence. But equally there has to be a sense of realism about the nature of the teams they’ve played. Brighton may have thrashed a shambolic Aston Villa 4-0 last weekend, but they were missing seven frontline players at Stamford Bridge and still put three past Chelsea on Sunday. And while Fulham looked very lively as Chelsea won 3-2 on the opening weekend, they couldn’t muster a shot on target against Sunderland on Sunday.

How good are Brighton? Were Villa just terrible on that first weekend? Was it really just Granit Xhaka’s appeal for Sunderland to be themselves again that made a side that had lost at Ipswich capable of dominating Fulham through midfield? It’s very hard at this stage to trace any patterns, other than perhaps to say that Xhaka’s performance against Fulham showed why Chelsea wanted to sign him in the summer.

The systems are different, so the comparison perhaps isn’t entirely fair, but Xhaka, and his midfield partner Noah Sadiki, offered a level of control that Chelsea under Alonso have so far been entirely lacking – striking, given the degree of control Enzo Maresca insisted upon as manager last season. Both Chelsea games so far have felt almost like a pastiche of the modern Bundesliga: all high tempo and turnovers, chaotic and fun and slightly unserious.

This is not how it’s meant to be. Alonso’s Bayer Leverkusen side, in which Xhaka was partnered in central midfield by one of Robert Andrich, Aleix García, or Exequiel Palacios, won the Bundesliga in 2024 conceding only 24 goals in 34 league games. They averaged 59.5% possession, whereas Chelsea so far this season have had just 32%. Perhaps when Moisés Caicedo returns to fitness – he managed 14 minutes from the bench on Sunday before being forced off again – his energy and mobility will bring an immediate improvement, but the way both Fulham and Brighton have at times sliced through Chelsea suggests there are structural issues.

The usual criticism of the 3-4-2-1 formation used by Chelsea is that it is too blockish, that creativity comes almost entirely from the two inside-forwards, making the side playing it predictable if they dominate possession. Its usage, at least in the Premier League, tends to have been as a counterattacking system – this is how, for instance, Oliver Glasner deployed it at Crystal Palace over the last two seasons. Two holding players operating in front of a back three should provide the trapezoid shape that has become the default for sides hoping to guard against the counter. Yet with Roméo Lavia alongside either Reece James or Malo Gusto, that solidity has been lacking.

Why, then, is Alonso’s system suffering the opposite problem? The issue really stems from a positive: Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 is not the blockish formation often seen. Rather it is a basis from which multiple variations stem. It has a variety that helps overcome a potential over-reliance on the two inside-forwards. That’s how, for instance, center back Maxence Lacroix ended up bursting through to set up a goal against Fulham. Breaking the lines and varying the pattern is part of the pattern.

The defensive concerns predate Alonso. It’s been 18 games since Chelsea last kept a clean sheet, their longest run in the top flight since 1961. While the signing of Emí Martínez should give them a more assertive, less error-prone figure in goal than Robert Sánchez in goal, there will be issues, at least in the short term, in getting the balance right at full-back. Plus, defences are best when they are stable, when interactions become automatic; while Lacroix is the sort of central defender Chelsea have been short of and will almost certainly make them better in the long term, and while Josh Acheampong, who played well against Fulham and came off the bench against Brighton, looks a hugely promising presence (he started only eight league games last season); incorporating both of them while adapting to a new goalkeeper will take time. There is a cost to the constant churn at Chelsea.
