Arsenal, next Sunday, will provide a far stiffer test. Chelsea’s front three of João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer give them a puncher’s chance, but there is a chance Arsenal render them irrelevant by dominating the game through the midfield. They are two teams at very different stages of their development.

Sports.title: Liverpool instantly reject ambitious £30m bid from Nottingham Forest for future star, 19
Sports.content:
Liverpool have reportedly rejected a bid from Nottingham Forest for midfielder Trey Nyoni.

A £30million offer was lodged for the 19-year-old ahead of Tuesday's transfer deadline.



3 Liverpool have rejected a £30m bid from Forest for Nyoni Credit: Getty

The deal would have seen Forest pay a guaranteed £25million with a further £5million in add-ons.

According to The Athletic, the Reds immediately rebuffed the approach.

Nyoni's Liverpool future

Nyoni is highly thought of at Anfield, with an exit this summer ruled out by the club.



Instead, Andoni Iraola expects the teenager to feature regularly this season, the report adds.

It comes after Liverpool decided against signing a replacement for Curtis Jones, who was sold to Inter Milan earlier this month.



Nyoni has been earmarked as a successor having joined the Reds' academy from Leicester City in 2023.

He has since made 21 first-team appearances for the club, with his Premier League debut coming in December aged 18.



Harvey Elliott has also moved on loan to Valencia in another midfield exit for Iraola.

A loan exit was previously decided against last summer with Nyoni instead seen as a first-team candidate despite his age.

Liverpool had previously handed Nyoni a five-year professional deal last summer which expires in 2030.

3 Nyoni is once again expected to feature for the first-team at Anfield this season Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, he was an unused substitute as the Reds beat Chelsea to win the Carabao Cup back in 2024 as a 16-year-old.

The England Under-19 international featured in Saturday's 2-2 draw with Forest, making a 13-minute cameo off the bench after replacing Alexis Mac Allister in midfield.

Victor Munoz subsequently grabbed the hosts' equaliser just five minutes after Nyoni was introduced.

Liverpool transfer latest

Barring any major outgoings, Liverpool are not expected to make any further signings before Tuesday's 11pm transfer deadline.



talkSPORT understands the Reds intend to keep hold of Cody Gakpo after rejecting an £80million bid from Manchester City.

Whilst they have been offered several midfielders ahead of deadline day, no deals are currently ongoing.

3 Iraola is not expected to make any further signings before the transfer deadline Credit: Getty

Iraola has spent over £200million this summer with the biggest purchase the £123million arrival of Bradley Barcola on Monday.

Sports.title: Champions League club explore audacious loan swoop for Arsenal star Ethan Nwaneri
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund are keen to sign Arsenal starlet Ethan Nwaneri, talkSPORT understands.

The German giants are eyeing a loan move for the 19-year-old before the transfer window closes.

3 Dortmund saw Nwaneri in full flow during the Emirates Cup this summer Credit: Getty

Bundesliga sides have until 7pm UK time on Tuesday to finalise their summer business, although the window being open in England would give them another four hours.

Dortmund have identified Nwaneri as a late target as they look to bolster their options for this season's Champions League.

They will face Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on November 24, although Nwaneri would be unlikely to be eligible to face his parent club should he make the move.

The midfielder was not included in the matchday squad for Arsenal's win over Aston Villa on Monday night.

He has yet to feature for the Gunners this term, having been an unused substitute against Coventry City in the season opener.

Nwaneri spent the second half of last season on loan at Marseille.

However, he made just 11 appearances for the club, scoring twice and adding an assist.

The teenager is the Premier League's youngest-ever player after making his debut aged 15 years and 181 days in September 2022.

Nwaneri has since featured 51 times for Arsenal following his progression from their famed Hale End academy.

Nwaneri's Arsenal future

talkSPORT revealed earlier this month that Nwaneri was expected to leave the Emirates Stadium before the end of the transfer window.

3 Nwaneri has yet to feature for Arsenal this season and is expected to leave the club Credit: Getty

It came after he was left out for their Community Shield victory over Manchester City.

Previous talks were held with Galatasaray before interest emerged from clubs in Germany.

As well as Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen have also been earmarked as a potential landing spot.

Dortmund are also set to face Aston Villa on the road along with home matches against Inter Milan, Real Betis and Villarreal.

Nwaneri made his first appearance in the competition as a 17-year-old back in November 2024.

To date, he has scored twice in ten Champions League outings for Arsenal.

Sports.title: Arsenal urged to complete late deal for Vinicius Jr alternative who rejected Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Lyon forward Malick Fofana has been offered to Arsenal, talkSPORT understands.

The Belgium international previously rejected a move to Hull City earlier in the summer.



3 Arsenal have been offered the chance to sign Lyon forward Fofana Credit: Getty

Roma and RB Leipzig have also been credited with interest in Fofana.

However, he could now complete a late switch to the Premier League champions.

The Gunners have until the window closes at 11pm on Tuesday to conclude their transfer business.

Having missed out on the signing of Vinicius Jr, adding another wide attacker remains under consideration.



Fofana's Lyon future is up in the air after the Ligue 1 side missed out on a place in the league phase of the Champions League.

They were beaten by Turkish giants Fenerbahce last week, causing them to drop into the Europa League.



The 21-year-old's current Lyon deal expires at the end of next season.

Since joining the club from Gent in 2024, he has scored 19 goals and added eight assists in 84 appearances across all competitions.



talkSPORT verdict

European football journalist Andy Brassell has tipped Fofana to be a success if he were to move to the Emirates Stadium.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT.com, he explained: "Straight off, ever since Lyon have been eliminated from the Champions League play-offs, they've had a lot of players on the block.

3 Vinicius Jr signed a new six-year deal with Real Madrid to end any hope of Arsenal landing him Credit: AFP

"They are not just willing to sell, they need to sell, and they need to make around €50million, before the window shuts.



"The quickest way of doing that, because they have at least one more definitely out already, is Malick Fofana.

"Obviously, he's been linked with a lot of different teams so far. Hull City made an approach and rejected that pretty much out of hand, slightly more politely perhaps.

"Linked to Roma for a number of weeks, seems like Leipzig might be in and there's even been talk in France that he's been offered to Arsenal.

"Now, even though he's not Vinicius Jr, clearly, I think him being offered to Arsenal is really interesting because he is a player exactly in the spot where they want a player.



"His ceiling is very, very high. He missed most of last season because of a really bad ankle injury that he received in the game against Strasbourg.

3 Fofana has been tipped to make an 'interesting' move to Arsenal before the window closes Credit: Getty

"He still had some pain when he came back, so it took a while for him to get that sorted out and since he has got that sorted out, he's been really good in the early part of this season for Lyon when he has played.

"I think he can add more goals to his game as well. He's got speed and he's really good at bringing the ball up the pitch quickly.



"I think he was clocked the season before the one he was injured in as the fastest player in Ligue 1. So, I think that's an interesting one for sure."

Arsenal have already spent over £200million on four new signings following their Premier League triumph last term.

Mikel Arteta's side ended their 22-year wait for a 14th league title victory.

They have since added Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Christos Tzolis to their ranks.



Meanwhile, Pieor Hincapie's loan from Bayer Leverkusen has been made permanent for £45million.

Several exits could still be finalised before the window closes, though, with deals involving Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus in the works.

Sports.title: Tottenham move for Iliman Ndiaye hijacked by Man City despite deal being agreed
Sports.content:
Tottenham move for Iliman Ndiaye hijacked by Man City despite deal being agreed

Manchester City have completed the signing of Iliman Ndiaye after Tottenham agreed a deal to sign him, talkSPORT understands.

Enzo Maresca's side have secured the services of the Everton forward in a £60million deal, with £5m in add-ons.

4 Ndiaye insisted on going to City once they revived their interest in him Credit: Getty

This is despite Spurs agreeing a £60m move with the Toffees, however, the player pushed for a switch to City.

Spurs' move being hijacked also appears to end any hope of striker Richarlison going back to Merseyside.

City pivoted towards Ndiaye having lost out on the signing of Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo.

City initially usurped Spurs in the race for Gakpo and were confident they would sign the Dutchman.

But talkSPORT understands Liverpool will only sanction a sale of Gakpo if they can sign another winger before Tuesday's deadline despite securing the services of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

Tottenham instigated a deal for Ndiaye, who famously knocked them out of the FA Cup in 2023 with Championship side Sheffield United.

The Senegalese star spent two years with Everton and etched his name in the history books by scoring the final two goals at Goodison Park in 2025.

The 26-year-old appeared in both the Toffees' games this season and got an assist against Crystal Palace in their 2-0 win in their first fixture.

Across all campaigns he managed a total of 20 goal contributions and Tottenham are now set to land him as they seek to improve their forward line.

He also managed one goal and two assists at the 2026 World Cup with his nation.

4 City are set for a very busy end to the transfer window Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands Ndiaye has turned down multiple contract offers from Everton over the past 12 months.

Richarlison looked set to go the other way, in a separate transfer and return to the club he left for £60million in 2022.

However, in a statement released on Monday, the player appeared to hit out at the club for the way they acted during the negotiations.

The Brazilian hit 53 goals in 152 appearances for The Toffees, becoming a fan favourite, before securing a move to the capital.

There, though, he spent much of his first campaign limited behind Harry Kane and beset by fitness issues.

This would be a common theme in north London, despite hitting 32 goals in all competitions while moving between centre-forward and left wing.

4 Spurs are back in the Premier League relegation zone after two games of the 2026/27 season Credit: Getty

Tottenham moved quickly in the summer transfer window after narrowly avoiding relegation.

They brought in Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100million, Mateus Fernandes from West Ham for £85m, and Jan Paul van Hecke for £52m.

This was swiftly followed by the free transfer signings of Andrew Robertson, Marcos Senesi, and Martin Dubravka.

After a long saga, Savio and Omar Marmoush then arrived from Man City last week with the former joining for £85m and the latter on loan with an obligation to buy for £60m.

4 Kevin Danso is also keen to depart the club Credit: Getty

However, they have lost their first two games of the season in a disappointing start to their new era.

A 4-0 loss to Brentford was followed by a 2-0 defeat to Newcastle.

An number of stars were left out, including Kevin Danso, Pape Matar Sarr, and Richarlison.

And De Zerbi addressed this after the Newcastle game.

"Richarlison, he's said too many times he wants to leave," the Spurs head coach said.

"Danso came to me two days ago, and he said he wants to leave.

"The other player, Sarr, is the same but he's suffered a small injury. But, he's almost ready to train."

He added: "I love these players, and they are great guys," the Italian explained. "I have very good relationships.

"But, if they want to leave, they have to bring the economic solution to the club and they can go, and we'll find other players."

Sports.title: Tottenham agree loan move with Chelsea for Mykhailo Mudryk with option to buy for huge £75m fee
Sports.content:
Tottenham agree loan move with Chelsea for Mykhailo Mudryk with option to buy for huge £75m fee

Tottenham have agreed a deal with Chelsea over the loan signing of Mykhailo Mudryk, talkSPORT understands.

The transfer will also include an option to make the winger's stay permanent at the end of the season for £75million.



6 Mudryk is free to play football once again after his doping ban was lifted Credit: Getty

Mudryk's Chelsea contract expires in 2031 having signed an eight-and-a-half year contract when joining from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023.

Spurs are trying to strengthen the wide attacking areas and have seen a few deals fall through, sparking a late shock move for Ukrainian winger Mudryk.

The 25-year-old is back from his doping ban after all charges were dropped against him earlier this summer.



However, he is yet to play a single minute of first-team football for the Blues since returning.

6



Xabi Alonso hasn't involved him in the Premier League or Carabao Cup so far, and Spurs are looking to reunite him with Roberto De Zerbi.

The duo worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk with Spurs also agreeing a deal with Chelsea to sign Tosin Adarabioyo on a permanent basis.



Mudryk has been the subject of interest from Sunderland, Leeds United and Coventry City.

Scrambling

It has been a dramatic 24 hours in the transfer market for Tottenham.

Spurs agreed a deal with Everton to sign Iliman Ndiaye with Richarlison heading back to the Toffees in a separate deal.

But in a shock twist, Manchester City came back in for Ndiaye to wrap up a move due to Liverpool calling off a deal for Cody Gakpo to go to Manchester City.

6 Tosin is set to leave Chelsea after two years at the club Credit: Getty



6 Ndiaye had looked to be heading to Tottenham, but Man City are back in Credit: Getty

Spurs had been keen on the Dutchman too but he favoured a move to the Etihad Stadium in the event of him leaving Liverpool.

However, the Reds haven't been able to find a replacement, with moves for Yankuba Minteh and Ismaila Sarr stalling.

And this means City turned attentions to Ndiaye and are understood to have completed the signing of him.



Enzo Maresca has been interested in the Senegalese international for some time, but they cooled their interest to focus on Gakpo.

But with Gakpo off the table, City went back in for Ndiaye with Jack Grealish potentially going the other way.

talkSPORT understands that Grealish would prefer a move to Everton over any other club this summer as well.

6 Richarlison threw some chaos in the air with his update on his future



Further complicating Spurs' deal for Ndiaye to join Spurs was Richarlison.

What has Richarlison done?

The Brazilian international was set to return to Everton, but in a bombshell series of Instagram stories, he appeared to suggest that he is staying put.

This comes despite him asking Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi to leave.

But he hit out at Spurs and suggested that he was being forced to leave not on his own terms despite wanting to return the Toffees.

The stories were in Portuguese, but they have been translated as follows.



"After everything I've been through in recent years, I decided that they would never again decide my future for me," he wrote.

6 Richarlison is going nowhere, or so it seems Credit: Getty

"I've been through a lot of bad things these days and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people.

"Pressure, threats, retaliations, none of this scares me. I've been through worse things… believe me!



"I have always made it clear, at every opportunity, that an exit of mine to another place would also have to be good for the club.

"If it wasn't, I would never accept… as I didn't accept when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.

"I stayed and gave my life. So, I hope you treat my situation with the same respect that I always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't want to decide for me.

"If they enter into an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I go back to my favourite team.



"My intention was to return to the place where I was very happy. But the negotiations were the way people wanted and it won't be like this anymore.

"Despite this riot, I have a contract with Spurs and I will be at the club's disposal."

Sports.title: Richarlison set to stay at Tottenham in shock U-turn as he furiously hits out in cryptic statement
Sports.content:
Richarlison set to stay at Tottenham in shock U-turn as he furiously hits out in cryptic statement

Richarlison all-but confirmed he will not be re-joining Everton from Tottenham Hotspur.

The striker had appeared set for a return to the Toffees ahead of the Premier League transfer deadline.



3 Richarlison has announced he will not be leaving Spurs to re-join Everton Credit: Getty

Clubs have until 11pm on Tuesday to conclude their summer business.

A deal between Everton and Spurs for Richarlison had been agreed alongside a separate transfer involving Iliman Ndiaye.

It came after Roberto De Zerbi had revealed the forward had asked to leave the club.

Manchester City have since hijacked Spurs' move for Ndiaye, ending any hope of Richarlison going back to Everton.



But before this emerged, Richarlison put out an explosive statement outlining the his frustration over the uncertainty around his future.

Richarlison statement

In a message posted on his Instagram story, the player appeared to hit out at Spurs for the way they've acted during the negotiations.



He wrote: "After everything I've been through in recent years, I decided that they would never again decide my future for me.

"I've been through a lot of bad things these days and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people.



"Pressure, threats, retaliations, none of this scares me. I've been through worse things… believe me!

"I have always made it clear, at every opportunity, that an exit of mine to another place would also have to be good for the club.

3 Richarlison released a furious statement on social media to confirm his future Credit: Getty

"If it wasn't, I would never accept… as I didn't accept when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.



"I stayed and gave my life. So, I hope you treat my situation with the same respect that I always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don't want to decide for me.

"If they enter into an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I go back to my favourite team.

"My intention was to return to the place where I was very happy. But the negotiations were the way people wanted and it won't be like this anymore.

"Despite this riot, I have a contract with Spurs and I will be at the club's disposal."



Richarlison previously spent four years at Everton after signing from Watford in 2018.

3 The Toffees had agreed a deal with Spurs to bring Richarlison back to the club Credit: Getty

During that time, he scored 53 goals in 152 appearances across all competitions.

Having moved to Spurs in 2022, the Brazil international was part of the side which won the Europa League last year.



The triumph ended the club's 17-year trophy drought with victory in the final over Manchester United.

The 29-year-old was not included in the matchday squad for Saturday's defeat to Newcastle United.

He started in a defeat against Brentford the previous week.

Sports.title: EFL forced to reschedule three matches as they launch scathing attack on UEFA over fixture chaos
Sports.content:
EFL forced to reschedule three matches as they launch scathing attack on UEFA over fixture chaos

The EFL has been forced into a fixture shake-up following confirmation of Liverpool's Champions League schedule.

A total of three matches have been moved in order to accommodate the Reds' European commitments.



3 The EFL have been forced to move two Carabao Cup ties due to UEFA's scheduling Credit: Getty

It follows the draw for the third round of this season's Carabao Cup.

Everton had been due to host Wolves on Wednesday, September 9.

However, UEFA have scheduled Liverpool's league phase opener against Atletico Madrid at Anfield for the same night.

Rules currently prevent both Merseyside clubs from playing at home on the same night.

As a result, the Toffees will now meet Wolves on Wednesday, September 16.



Meanwhile, Liverpool's own third round tie, a home clash with Tottenham Hotspur will be played the day before at 8pm.

A third fixture has also been moved in order to accommodate the Carabao Cup matches.



Wolves had previously been set to host Portsmouth in the Championship at Molineux on September 9.

The fixture was pushed back to September 16 after their trip to Everton was given a date.



That Championship match will now be played at 7:45pm on Tuesday, October 20.

3 Wolves' Carabao Cup tie away to Everton has been rescheduled to September 16 Credit: Getty

EFL statement

In a statement confirming the news, the EFL said: "The EFL has been left with no option than to rearrange a number of its fixtures following the announcement of fixture details for the league phase of the UEFA Champions League.

"On 28 August, we confirmed that the Carabao Cup Round Three tie between Everton and Wolves had been scheduled for Wednesday 9 September.



"This was confirmed with local stakeholders as per usual practice ahead of announcement.

"On Saturday, UEFA announced that it had scheduled Liverpool v Atletico Madrid for the same date, despite it being clear that Everton and Liverpool cannot play home fixtures on the same evening.

"The EFL met with UEFA officials on Monday morning to explore available options, however in those discussions it was made clear that they were unwilling to consider rescheduling the Liverpool v Atletico Madrid fixture, and avoiding the consequences for other fixtures as a result."

The EFL added: "Over recent seasons the League has made a number of changes to accommodate the expansion of UEFA club competitions – a decision which was made without adequate consultation with domestic leagues.



3 Liverpool's home match against Atletico Madrid has caused the EFL a fixture headache Credit: getty

"These changes have included splitting Carabao Cup Round Three ties across two weeks, and implementing draw conditions for Round Three which prevent scheduling conflicts for clubs playing in the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League.

"This makes UEFA’s unwillingness to cooperate all the more frustrating, not least for the supporters of the five clubs that will now be inconvenienced as a result."

A separate statement from Portsmouth explained: "The knock-on effect of this is that disappointingly, our visit to Molineux has been postponed for a second time and will now take place on Tuesday, October 20 (7.45pm kick-off).



"Due to the extremely late notice of these changes, Wolves are unable to host the game on the original date of September 9.

"Portsmouth Football Club are extremely frustrated that our fans, many of whom will have twice made arrangements for this game, are adversely affected."

Pompey had only announced the previous date change for their trip to Wolves on Friday.

Sports.title: Cody Gakpo transfer decision made as Man City submit £80m bid to Liverpool
Sports.content:
Liverpool have rejected an £80million bid for Cody Gakpo from Manchester City, talkSPORT understands.

The forward is now set to remain at Anfield beyond Tuesday's 11pm transfer deadline.



3 Liverpool have rejected an £80million bid for Gakpo from City Credit: Getty

It is the Reds' intention to keep hold of Gakpo, with an exit never guaranteed to be sanctioned despite the player being open to a move.

A deadline day departure is unlikely due to the lack of time left for Liverpool to sign a replacement.

Their need to bring in a successor is seen as a key stumbling block as opposed to the financials of a potential deal.



As for City, they intend to complete the signing of Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

A move for Iliman Ndiaye could also be pursued despite a deal being agreed between Tottenham Hotspur and Everton for the playmaker.



Gakpo's Liverpool future

Gakpo started, and got an assist, in Liverpool's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

However, with Bradley Barcola coming into the club there has been speculation over his future.



Tottenham have been the club showing the most interest in Gakpo this summer.

But now City have ramped up their pursuit of the Dutch international in recent days.

Despite formal talks with Liverpool over a deal, though, their offer has been knocked back.

3 Iraola could have a busy last few days of the window Credit: Getty



talkSPORT verdict

Speaking on Saturday, talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs said: “Manchester City in the last few days have gone really big on Cody Gakpo. It's taken the player a little bit by surprise because for much of the summer, it was Tottenham and Cody Gakpo. He’d spoken to Roberto De Zerbi.

“But our information is that Cody Gakpo favours Manchester City.

“As a consequence, this is expected to develop. I actually think that Tottenham now realise they can't do that deal. Do they turn to Iliman Ndiaye as a result?

“Bradley Barcola comes in, as we exclusively revealed this morning, for £106million with £17million in add-ons.

“It may come down to the player realising even if they don't add now another attacker, Victor Munoz has come in and Rio Ngumoha needs a pathway.



"Gakpo maybe in previous seasons could have looked out wide, looked in the centre. But now up front, it's Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitike. Behind them, it's Florian Wirtz.

3 Gakpo is a Premier League winner with Liverpool Credit: AFP

“So I think he seems to believe that even if it's not now, it might be the beginning of the end.

“This was kind of what Luis Diaz thought when Liverpool wanted to keep the player, but eventually they sold him to Bayern Munich.



“Cody Gakpo has got a big decision to make. From Liverpool's perspective, if they were to sell, they know they're bringing in more money.

“It might mean that they can overpay for an Ismaïla Sarr or a Yankuba Minteh. Then two attackers will come in as well.”

The 27-year-old signed for Liverpool from PSV in 2023 for around £44m.

He signed a new long-term contract with the club last summer.

Gakpo also has 51 goals in 182 games in all competitions for the club.



More Liverpool signings?

Asked by talkSPORT's Sam Matterface after his side's 2-2 home draw with Nottingham Forest whether he'd be happy with his squad should the Barcola deal go through, Iraola said: "I think now we need to be patient. We don't know what's going to happen.

"There are still some days [left] in the market and obviously there are going to be movements. We will need to analyse when this happens.

"I'm looking forward to being in the second half of September and knowing what we have, and then making definitive plans with this.

"But the competition works like this – the rules are the same for everyone.



"It's uncomfortable in terms of uncertainty until the market closes, but now it's just a matter of a couple of days, so we will wait."

Sports.title: Callaway and Good Good executives axed amid fallout after controversial ad which 'depicted domestic violence'
Sports.content:
Callaway and Good Good executives axed amid fallout after controversial ad which 'depicted domestic violence'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The fallout from the Callaway/Good Good ad controversy continues as executives at both companies have been let go in the aftermath of the 'tone deaf' commercial.

Good Good, the popular YouTube channel and golf brand, has lost endorsement deals and media opportunities after they produced a commercial for a branded driver which critics say depicted domestic violence.

In response, Callaway ended their partnership with the group. Additionally, Good Good has had their products pulled off shelves, their show with Golf Channel has been cancelled before it even began and the brand backed out of their title sponsorship of a tournament in Austin.

Now, further consequences have been revealed after both Good Good and Callaway are ousting executives.

According to Front Office Sports, Alex Upegui, Callaway's director of content and production, is leaving the company.

Upegui is believed to be the highest-ranking Callaway employee who would have had the authority to approve the ad. He had been in his position since 2023.

Fallout continues amid the Good Good/Callaway ad controversy that gripped the two brands

Alex Upegui, Callaway's director of content and production, is leaving the company

Good Good is also firing their VP of brand and marketing, Jeffrey Lefkovits

Additionally, the outlet reports that Good Good's VP of brand and marketing, Jeffrey Lefkovits, has been fired.

FOS also reports that another unnamed Good Good employee is being let go.

In a statement on August 25, Callaway CEO Chip Brewer said the company was 'conducting both internal and external investigations and have already made changes to our approval process aimed at ensuring this will never happen again.'

Two days after that statement, Callaway announced they were severing ties with the golf brand, saying: 'In this instance, our content review process was not comprehensive enough. We have taken appropriate internal corrective actions and significantly strengthened our approval procedure to help ensure this does not happen again.'

The full-60 second ad, for the Good Good-branded Callaway Quantum driver, was supposed to be a spoof of the popular horror movie 'Obsession.'

But the opening of the  shows Good Good co-founder Clark rushing over and body-checking fellow member Alexis Miestowski as she reached for the golf club.

As Miestowski lay flat on her back on the ground, Clark is seen standing over her before angrily saying: 'Do not touch my new driver.'

The rest of the ad shows other members of the content team somehow becoming possessed by the golf club before the video ends.

The video depicts Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark body-checking collaborator Alexis Miestowski to the ground as she attempted to reach for a branded driver

The popular golf social media brand has seen backlash from fans and sponsors over the ad

In a video released following the backlash, Clark apologized and even called the commercial the 'worst ad known to man.'

Last week, Kendrick told the Wall Street Journal: 'We fully own that we did make a mistake … As the CEO of the company, the buck stops with me and we should have had better processes in place.'

He added: 'Obviously the execution missed the mark and didn’t come across the way that we wanted to, and in no way were we trying to make light of or support violence. But it came across that way, and that’s our fault.'

But the apologies have not prevented Good Good's empire from crumbling.

The Golf Channel announced that the upcoming show, 'Good Good x Big Break,' has been canceled – just 24 hours after initially announcing that it was only pushing back the release by a week.

The decision to delay the release came after an unnamed sponsor, believed to be Golf Magic, asked for its branding to be removed from the show. But The Golf Channel has now made the decision to scrap the show altogether.

Big Break is golf's version of a reality TV show, pitting 12 aspiring golfers against each other in a series of unusual challenges, with players eliminated each week until only one winner remains.

Garrett Clark posted his own apology video after the disastrous Callaway advert was pulled

It ran for 23 seasons from 2003 to 2015 before being canceled, but was set to make its big return this year in a partnership with Good Good. The show was due to be hosted by professional golfer and model Blair O'Neal and TV host Wells Adam.

The winner of the 2026 reboot was due to receive an exemption into the PGA Tour's Good Good Championship in November – but the Good Good branding has now been pulled from that event.

'The PGA TOUR has been informed of Good Good Golf's decision to step away as sponsor of the event in Austin, Texas, this fall,' a statement read.

On the PGA Tour's website, the event is now titled the Austin Championship, with no sign of Good Good as the tour evaluates its ongoing partnership with the YouTubers.

Sports.title: Dark past behind Aryna Sabalenka's secret weapon: Death and the California desert haunt her coach as she chases US Open history
Sports.content:
Dark past behind Aryna Sabalenka's secret weapon: Death and the California desert haunt her coach as she chases US Open history

Jason Stacy’s eyes begin to glisten as his mind drifts from this New York bar back to Edwards Air Force Base in the California desert. To a night in front of the TV with his father.

‘I was maybe eight years old,’ Stacy recalls. ‘He literally had a knife poking toward my ribs.’ He wipes his eyes, apologizes and adds: ‘I don't think about it too much.’

It is a few days before the start of the US Open and Stacy is in Midtown Manhattan, charting his remarkable journey from that airbase to the summit of women’s tennis. These days, he serves as high performance coach of Aryna Sabalenka, the world No 1 who arrives in New York chasing a third successive title.

There is science behind his methods, which help Sabalenka cope with both the rigors of Grand Slam tennis and all the off-court commitments that come with being a superstar. Sometimes his advice is to focus on the feeling of her toes; occasionally they will prepare for matches with a game of tic-tac-toe on his bald head.

But Stacy also leans on lessons mined from a punishing life. He was born in Japan before moving to the United States. His father died in his arms when he was 11. By 13, he was homeless, alone on the streets in Tacoma, Washington, where he was stabbed and shot at and held at gunpoint. He watched two friends die by suicide; he would hang outside bakeries 'just to breathe in the smell of fresh bread.'

‘It has everything to do with how I am and who I am right now,’ Stacy says.

Jason Stacy serves as high performance coach of world No 1 tennis star Aryna Sabalenka

Sabalenka and Stacy have employed some quirky methods since they began working together

That night when his dad pressed a knife into his skin is, in fact, one of the less traumatic tales - they were watching police drama ‘Hill Street Blues’ when the topic of rape came up. Stacy asked what that meant, so his father decided to show him how to deal with a rapist. ‘This is how you would puncture their lungs,' he recalls. 'So they would drown in their own blood and not be able to yell out.’

Stacy's father died from a blood clot following a motorcycle accident. His young son tried in vain to keep him breathing. Before long, the teenager was separated from his mother and siblings, too, and on a dangerous downward spiral.

After several years on the streets, Stacy sought sanctuary in a library - poring over old newspaper cuttings, burying himself in books on space and history - and in a dojo, where he rose to become a black belt in jiu-jitsu.

These days, his focus is bringing Sabalenka to the boil four fortnights a year. In a sport where some rivals change coaches almost as often as they change ends, their partnership has endured since 2018.

At first, his work centered around Sabalenka's fitness; coach Anton Dubrov has handled the tennis since 2020. Now, though, Stacy has been christened the de facto CEO of Team Sabalenka.

Together, they have won four Grand Slam singles titles and Sabalenka could soon become the first woman since Serena Williams to win three straight titles at Flushing Meadows.

But the 28-year-old can be combustible and Sabalenka’s position as world No 1 is under threat after a testing, tempestuous few months. She has reached only one semifinal since March and recent Grand Slams have brought shock defeats followed by a desire to ‘get completely drunk’ and even 'quit tennis right now.' These are the times when Stacy earns his money.

Some of his techniques won’t be found in traditional coaching manuals - at the 2024 US Open, Stacy vowed to put a temporary version of Sabalenka’s tiger tattoo on his head if she made the final.

‘We were eating food right before the match… and I pulled out the tattoo,’ Stacy recalls. Sabalenka had completely forgotten. But he told her: ‘I made a promise.’ The Belarusian went on to beat Jessica Pegula in straight sets.

Sabalenka has won four Grand Slam singles titles including at the 2024 and 2025 US Open

While some players routinely change coaches, their partnership has endured since 2018

In 2024, Stacy vowed to put a version of Sabalenka’s tattoo on his head if she made the final

Sabalenka's tiger tattoo pictured in 2023 in a Wimbledon first-round clash

Many of the American's methods are detailed in his new book, ‘The Pressure Code’

Over the years, he has learned to spot small tells in Sabalenka’s behavior. If conversation begins veering from topic to topic, for instance, Stacy knows he needs to narrow the world No 1's attention.

‘I would, let's say, create a drill or an exercise that literally forces her to focus on a spot while she's doing a certain movement,’ he says. ‘To quiet all that noise… usually that's all it takes.’

Many of Stacy’s methods are detailed in his new book, ‘The Pressure Code,’ which explains the importance of ‘aligning’ energy, emotions and environment. The principles, Stacy writes, apply to those battling to become world No 1 and those hoping to improve their everyday life.

The book is centered around Stacy’s fall and rise. With a father in the US Air Force, the family hopped around from Japan to Germany to bases in the US. Then his father died and, before long, Stacy was on the streets.

His life fit inside one backpack and, as he survived on the outskirts of Seattle, one piece of fatherly advice never left the teenager: don’t do drugs. He never crossed that red line, even after it landed him in trouble; Stacy says he suffered three concussions from being struck in the head with a gun.

He isn’t in touch with anyone from those days. ‘Probably most are dead anyway,’ Stacy says. And among the few keepsakes he has kept hold of? ‘My birth certificate,’ he explains. ‘When I was homeless, for some reason I had it… it's all falling apart and disintegrated.’

Stacy recently moved back to the States after more than a decade in Australia and he now lives close to Tacoma. He has driven by his old haunts. ‘It’s so weird,’ he says. That library is still standing and Stacy has reconnected with his estranged family via social media.

‘My younger sister died a long time ago. My brother's still around, and my mother - they're not too far from where I am,’ he says. ‘I'll probably go see them at some point.’

His father died in his arms when he was 11 and by 13 he was homeless on the streets of Tacoma

Stacy is hoping to guide Sabalenka to a third successive US Open title at Flushing Meadows

The dojo where he found 'salvation' was sandwiched between a pawn shop and an adult bookstore. Day after day, he would stare inside. Eventually he decided to walk in and before long, Stacy was invited to train and even stay for free.

From there, Stacy clambered back to his feet, sometimes while juggling multiple jobs. Some days, he would work at the pawn shop before training fighters and then carrying out maintenance work at McDonald’s. By the time he’d finished, it was back to the pawn shop. Days would go by without sleep. He still doesn’t get much - five or six hours on a good night - but thankfully his work now brings more handsome rewards.

Before joining Team Sabalenka, Stacy trained as a personal trainer, a massage therapist, a sports therapist, an athletic trainer and as a strength and conditioning coach. He has studied nutrition, psychology, philosophy, history. But he never stopped listening to his gut.

‘It tells me a lot about people, their intentions, about what might be happening,’ he says. Those were skills he honed in life-or-death situations on the streets.

Stacy has also worked with Olympians and athletes across jiu-jitsu, judo and swimming. So how does Sabalenka compare? ‘They're all a little bit crazy,’ he says. And there is another ‘common thread.’

‘When someone has a biggest strength of theirs, when they don't manage it well… [it] can also become the biggest weakness,' he says. 'They'll either climb the mountain or they're going to destroy themselves.’

Sabalenka’s career could have unraveled when, a few years back, her serve imploded. The 28-year-old could have crumbled in 2019, when meningitis killed her father Sergey. Or in March 2024, when her ex-boyfriend died in an apparent suicide.

Instead, she is back in New York chasing a third US Open title in a row. Who knows what pranks her team will come up with this year.

‘None of this stuff's ever been planned,’ Stacy says. ‘We spend all year just focused on performing your best, recovering great, all these things… [but] she's a human before she's a tennis player. And we all need to have those moments where we can just enjoy ourselves.’

Sports.title: Wild US Open clip goes viral as female player is spotted obliterating her racket in furious outburst... while her opponent celebrates just yards away
Sports.content:
French tennis star Lois Boisson has gone viral after furiously destroying her racket following her defeat to American star Emma Navarro in the first round of the US Open.

Boisson, 23, was sent crashing out of the competition after a 7-6, 6-7, 6-3 defeat to her US counterpart on Monday afternoon - and refused to hide her emotions after.

After the two players shook hands, Boisson immediately began taking her frustrations out on her own racket, smashing it into the ground numerous times.

Meanwhile, in the same frame, Navarro was waving to the crowd as they cheered on the American star after booking her place in the next round.

It appeared that Navarro was unaware of Boisson's fury following the result.

Their first round match had initially begun on Sunday before being postponed due to rain that hit the area, forcing outdoor action to be paused.

French tennis star Lois Boisson has gone viral after smashing her racket after her defeat

Boisson, 23, was sent crashing out of the competition after a 7-6, 6-7, 6-3 defeat to Navarro

'It was really tough stopping at the point of the match we were at,' Navarro said.

'I just felt like I had worked really hard to get to that point, and then all of a sudden, it's like we're gonna come out tomorrow and we both have a clean slate. It's it's really unique because you feel like you should feel like you're ahead, but you kind of don't.'

Navarro had been leading the contest prior to the match being postponed and managed to hold on despite a rejuvenated Boisson in her way.

'It was really tough. Kind of took me a little while to find my bearings,' Navarro said.

'I think it was after I got broken in the third when I was like, okay, now I'm klnow I'm where I want to be. I'm ready to play.'

The American star will now face the winner of Catherine McNally and Anouk Koevermans' match, which takes place later on Monday afternoon.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta leaves door open for Arsenal to sign a forward on deadline day amid lengthy pursuit of Julian Alvarez: 'If we can improve the squad, we will'
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta left the door open for Arsenal to make a deadline day move for a forward as they continue to monitor Julian Alvarez.

The champions recorded their second straight win at the start of their Premier League title defence, as Bukayo Saka’s second-half goal was enough to seal a 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

Arsenal have pursued Alvarez all summer. The Atletico Madrid forward would like to move to Barcelona but club chiefs have said they will not sell him to their La Liga rivals – opening the door for a potential £130million move.

‘If we can improve the squad we will,’ he said. ‘The depth has to be really big when we are fighting in four competitions so we are going to try to do that.’

Asked directly about Alvarez, Arteta said: ‘I don't know. That's for the people upstairs.’

Arsenal transfer chief Andrea Berta brought Alvarez to Atletico Madrid from Manchester City and has dreamed all summer of signing him for a second time.

Arsenal transfer chief Andrea Berta brought Alvarez to Atletico Madrid from Manchester City and has dreamed all summer of signing him for a second time

Whether Alvarez arrives or not, Arsenal look formidable and were always the better side against Aston Villa on Monday night

Whether Alvarez arrives or not, Arsenal look formidable. They were always the better side against Villa and saw out the game comfortably – in sharp contrast to last season, when Emi Buendia won it for Unai Emery’s men in stoppage time.

Arsenal looked distraught when that goal went in and Arteta revealed he has used those memories to inspire his team.

He said: ‘We used what happened last year to bring more energy, conviction and belief – that image of the players on the floor totally gutted. When we had to be dominant and had to suffer we did both and I’m very pleased.’

Even though this was better from Villa after their 4-0 hammering at Brighton on the opening day, they are still without a point or a goal in their opening two matches.

Emery handed debuts to goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and forward Nicolas Jackson and would hope to include fellow signings Ibrahim Mbaye, Leon Goretzka and Taylor Harwood-Bellis at Hull.

Emery said: ‘They are favourites to win the Premier League and we are trying to build a team, but a lot of positive things. The first step forward today is positive.

‘To lose is painful, but after we must try to get positive things. This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches. After two matches, we don't have a point but hopefully we can get better.

‘We can feel confident after this result because of the way we want to build a team again.’

Sports.title: Stefanos Tsitsipas reveals he had heard about Nick Kyrgios' 'behaviour' away from court before tennis firebrand was handed cocaine ban: 'I'm only surprised it came so late'
Sports.content:
Stefanos Tsitsipas admitted that he was not shocked by Nick Kyrgios' failed drugs test after the tennis firebrand was sanctioned for testing positive for cocaine, revealing that he was only surprised that it 'came so late'.

Kyrgios attempted to get ahead of a public announcement that he had failed a test during a tournament in Mallorca in June, and called upon his followers to understand the 'context' for the lapse came against the backdrop of his struggle to come to terms with the end of his injury-stricken career.

But Tsitsipas had a less charitable view when asked about Kyrgios' ban after his first-round victory against Arthur Fils at the US Open.

'I don't know what to tell you,' the Greek No1 said with a smile as he was asked if he had been surprised when news broke earlier this month. 'I mean, to be entirely honest with you, I knew about this before the announcement. Myself, I knew about it.

'So what can I tell you? I will just tell you the truth. I knew about all of this before any announcement was made, and when I saw it on social media, I was, like, "Here we go." I kind of expected it, to be honest.

When pushed further, Tsitsipas continued: 'I knew that those were things that were happening away from the tennis courts. I will tell you that.

Stefanos Tsitsipas admitted that he had not been surprised by news that Nick Kyrgios had tested positive for cocaine

'I'm not going to try and cover up someone that I know the truth for. I'll consider myself a nice person with everyone, but these were behaviours that I personally heard on the tour and heard other people in that same environment saying those sort of things to me.

'Again, when I saw it, I was, like, "Well, pretty much expected", to be honest. I am surprised it came so late, though.'

Kyrgios' representatives have been contacted by Daily Mail Sport for comment.

Tensions have long been high between the two players, with Tsitsipas clashing with Kyrgios at Wimbledon in 2022. Following their on-court tussle, the Greek referred to his Australian opponent as a 'bully' with an 'evil side'.

In response, Kyrgios claimed that his rival had 'serious issues.'

Kyrgios had been banned since August 4, sharing on social media that he took 'full responsibility' for the mistake 15 days later.

At that point, he had not registered an appeal, but when formally handed a ban, 31-year-old Kyrgios could face between three months and four years away from the sport.

A longer ban could be reduced should Kyrgios be able to prove that he did not use the substance for performance-enhancing purposes.

Kyrgios has battled persistent injury for recent years, and before his sanction, was some way from his career-high world No13 ranking.

Now ranked 919, Kyrgios had not won a singles match since the 2025 Miami Open.

Former British star Dan Evans, who retired this summer, was handed a one-year ban in 2017 after testing positive for cocaine at the Barcelona Open.

The drug had been found in the pocket of his washbag but the International Tennis Federation accepted his explanation that he had been contaminated after the drug found its way onto his finger or medication in the bag accidentally.

Sports.title: What Sydney Swans stripper believes caused her 'medical episode' that saw hotel party spill into chaos - and how an AFL star came to her aid as the 'Pullman Five' panicked
Sports.content:
More details are emerging about the wild stripper party that ended with five Sydney Swans players being stood down and barred from the Brownlow - including fresh claims regarding the 'medical episode' allegedly suffered by one of the dancers.

A source with knowledge of the events alleges another Swans player, not believed to be one of the so-called 'Pullman Five', came to the woman's aid after she fled into the hotel hallway in the early hours of August 17, a detail not previously reported.

The Daily Mail revealed last week how the night after Sydney's win over Essendon at the MCG descended into chaos when a small group of players hired female entertainers from the 'Party Girls Melbourne' agency to celebrate.

As dawn broke, teammates, coaches and club officials began gathering in the Pullman East Melbourne foyer in official club attire ahead of the team's flight home. Families, couples and business travellers were also checking out of the hotel.

Upstairs, however, the situation on the eighth floor was beginning to unravel.

Unbeknownst to club officials, one of the three women paid to perform private lap dances for the players had become unwell and was suffering from what she believes was carbon dioxide poisoning.

It has been confirmed that Swansmen Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Riley Bice were at the party. They were stood down and banned from the Brownlow Medal

The so-called 'Pullman Five' allegedly panicked as one of the exotic dancers, who believed that she was suffering from carbon dioxide poisoning due to the stuffy hotel room, dashed into the hallway topless. (Isaac Heeney is pictured with his fiancée Steffie Waters)

The Daily Mail previously revealed how the night after Sydney's win over Essendon at the MCG descended into chaos when a small group of players hired female entertainers to attend the Pullman East Melbourne hotel (pictured)

In the hours beforehand, the women had been negotiating fees for dances and bottom slaps with a group they believed were tradesmen after allegedly being told the men were 'carpenters'.

Eventually, the trio would make their way downstairs, where the sea of red jackets and AFL logos would confirm their clients weren't chippies but well-paid footballers.

This discovery, coupled with the dancer's medical episode, sparked tensions in the lobby as the women made a beeline for coach Dean Cox to complain.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon were subsequently stood down for the remainder of the AFL season.

The Mail can now reveal details of how the women came to arrive at the hotel in the middle of the night, after one of the five men made a booking with the agency.

Remarkably, we have been told that one of the three women wasn't actually a stripper by trade, and was simply on a night out with her friend, who received the job offer.

'The job was listed in a WhatsApp group chat [of adult entertainers] and requested two girls at the hotel,' a source with knowledge of the matter told the Mail.

'One of the dancers accepted it and told the agent that she would take her mate [who wasn't a stripper] along because she wanted to get into the industry anyway.

'She felt sick during the party and she actually thinks it was carbon dioxide poisoning because there were so many people crammed into one room and there wasn't enough fresh air,' claimed the insider. (Pictured: A generic photo of a hotel room at the Pullman East Melbourne)

According to the insider, an argument broke out after the men asked the dancer to step back inside and put some clothes on. She was later found by another player sitting by the lifts in the hallway. (Pictured: A generic photo of a corridor at the Pullman East Melbourne hotel)

The Mail has been told that one of the three women wasn't actually a stripper, and was simply on a night out with her friend, who received the job offer via the Party Girls Melbourne agency. (Pictured: the Party Girls website which uses stock imagery, not photos of the actual strippers)

'The agent disagreed and said she had already booked the second girl, who was one of her regulars, but she ended up just bringing her mate anyway.'

This meant that three women eventually arrived at the hotel rather than the two requested by the agency.

As the Mail previously reported, the night's entertainment started pleasantly enough.

'Everyone was just chatting to start with and they [the women] asked what they did for work because there were so many of them staying at the same hotel and nine of them crammed into one room [at one stage].'

The other four men mentioned by the source have yet to be identified, but there is no suggestion of any wrongdoing by them.

Indeed, a club spokesman confirmed last week: 'The Sydney Swans can confirm that all investigations carried out by the club have consistently indicated that the only representatives of the club in the room central to the police investigation were the five players who have been stood down.'

The source went on to claim: 'They [the players] said they were carpenters and working in the area.'

Because of their trade, 'the girls agreed to charge $200 per girl for a lap dance [performance] across all the guys,' they added.

'The girls performed to one song each and moved between the guys.'

It was shortly after the performers had finished their lap dance routine moving between the men that one of the women began feeling unwell. (Stock image posed by model)

'All five players were high profile and some were in relationships,' said the source. 'They really didn't want to be seen drinking in hotel rooms with strippers during footy season because they had a lot to lose.' (Pictured: Isaac Heeney with his fiancée Steffie Waters)

The source said this kind of performance would usually cost between $250 and $300, on top of the agency's standard booking fee.

'But because it was late and they didn't think [the men] earned much, they did them a deal and they just wanted to get the job done and leave,' the insider added.

The men paid on the spot and some physical contact was allowed while the dance was taking place, the source claimed.

According to the source, some of the men were 'wasted', swaying and unsteady on their feet, as the girls shimmied through their routines.

At one stage, a woman said that if the players wanted to touch the dancers, they would have to pay more.

'One guy agreed to pay an extra $50 to slap her a**e three times,' said the source.

It was shortly after the performers had finished their lap dance routine moving between the men that one of the women began feeling unwell.

While the father of the woman in question has previously indicated she suffered from an asthma attack, the Mail's source now claims something else entirely.

'She felt sick during the party and she actually thinks it was carbon dioxide poisoning because there were so many people crammed into one room and there wasn't enough fresh air,' claimed the insider.

While it is theoretically possible to suffer ill effects from elevated carbon dioxide levels in a crowded, poorly ventilated room, serious cases are considered rare and are more commonly associated with confined spaces where fresh air is limited.

Regardless of what caused her distress, the situation escalated when the woman rushed to the door, flung it open and leaned topless into the corridor in search of fresh air. The mood inside the room changed instantly, claimed the source.

'All five players were high profile and some were in relationships,' they said.

'They really didn't want to be seen drinking in hotel rooms with strippers during footy season because they had a lot to lose.'

According to the insider, an argument broke out after the men asked the dancer to step back inside and put some clothes on. She then wrapped herself in a hotel dressing gown and left the room, but ended up sitting on the floor by the lifts.

It was at this point that another Swans player, who the source indicated may not have been one of the five players named in connection with the hotel incident, was walking down the hallway and saw the woman in distress.

'He found her and asked if she was OK,' said the source.

This viral WhatsApp message purports to show the fraught scene in the Pullman East hotel foyer on the morning of Monday, August 17

The women confronted one of the club bosses in the lobby. Previous reports indicate that the representative they spoke to was coach Dean Cox, who is not accused of any wrongdoing

'He was pretty shocked when she told him she had been booked by some guys at a party, and he helped her up and walked her back to the room where the others were.'

The three women then made their way downstairs, where the situation began to attract even more attention.

In the lobby, the woman suffering the suspected medical episode said that she felt dizzy and couldn't breathe. She tried using an asthma pump, although it is not known if it was hers or one supplied by another person.

Her presence soon became noticeable as she waved her arms around and walked in and out of the hotel in search of fresh air, the source alleged.

Meanwhile, her friend went back upstairs to collect their belongings left behind at the party.

As more Swans players and staff began gathering in the lobby, the woman's friend returned from the eighth floor and it was only then that she realised why the 'Pullman Five' had been so desperate to keep the situation private: they were AFL players.

It was at this point that the women confronted one of the club bosses. Previous reports indicate that the representative they spoke to was coach Cox, who is not accused of any wrongdoing.

In a remarkable turn of events, a woman at the hotel who was unaware of the drama unfolding around her allegedly approached star player Heeney, whose hood was pulled up, and politely asked him to pose for a photo with her child.

Heeney obliged, claimed the source, but asked her not to use the camera flash.

Unbeknownst to the mother, the photo also captured one of the women in the background during the heated exchange with a club official.

As the bizarre scene continued to unravel, more guests began to take notice of what was going on. At least one person present in the lobby took a photo, which was later widely circulated on WhatsApp.

'I'm at the Pullman in Melbourne and three girls [are] getting kicked out... And one of them said to the guy, "We have everything recorded,"' read the viral message.

Heeney's fiancée Steffie Waters was seen looking stressed while speaking on the phone in Noosa on August 21. She was later pictured in happier spirits during a trip to the beach

The women made calls to their agent as well as police and, according to the source, were eventually asked to leave the hotel.

The dramatic scenes at the hotel were followed by serious allegations the next day.

Two women made police complaints alleging sexual assault. Later in the week, the third woman also made a police report with similar claims.

The Daily Mail does not suggest any of the named Swans players are under police investigation or involved in any wrongdoing alleged by the women.

No charges have been laid.

The Mail also understands that all three women, who have separately engaged civil lawyers, were told by police they were not allowed to have any contact with one another while investigations were ongoing.

When contacted for comment on Monday, Victoria Police said there was no update.

Sports.title: Arthur Fery admits watching the US Open used to be 'a little painful' - as British No1 prepares for his main draw debut after meteoric Wimbledon rise
Sports.content:
What a difference a year makes. This week, 12 months ago, British No1 Arthur Fery was decompressing at home after winning a Challenger event, the level one step below the elite ATP tour, in Barranquilla, Colombia.

He was preparing for another Challenger, held the following week in the sleepy French Riviera town of Cassis. Then ranked the mid-300s, he couldn’t remember if he had even watched the US Open. If he did, it wasn’t a comfortable experience.

‘It’s a little bit painful seeing all the guys your age who you were playing with in juniors playing the US Open, and you’re playing Challengers, or you’re injured,’ Fery admitted. ‘It’s not really jealousy, because you know that they deserved it, and you haven’t, because you’re at a lower ranking. But your competitive side wants to be there as well.

‘During my injury (two years ago), I transitioned to being stuck on that kind of sentiment to fully letting go at some point, and being like, “this is what it is”. I’ve dropped in the rankings, but I know why.’

Two years later, and the 24-year-old was a hair-breadth from a seeding in Flushing Meadows, and comes into his first-round meeting with world No14 Lorenzo Musetti on Tuesday fresh from a tour-level final at last weekend’s Winston-Salem Open.

'I can see now how that was the case a little bit,' Fery added, when asked if his run in North Carolina had shown those who wondered if his Wimbledon streak had been a lightning-strike. 'It's nice, but in the moment or beforehand, not so much. I didn't feel like I had to prove anything to anyone.

Arthur Fery used to find it almost painful to watch his peers at Grand Slams - now, he has made the main draw for the US Open

'I didn't put my expectations too high after Wimbledon. I was just giving myself time to grow into the player that I am, and the status that I now I have, being top 40 and playing these tournaments. I think that helped with playing well last week and making the final.

'Now in hindsight, I can see how there were obviously people who were waiting to see how I was going to do and if it was a one-off or a fluke whatever. But no, I think my expectations stay the same, and of myself, and just move forward and do the best I can.'

Fery enjoyed 12 tennis-free days after his semi-final in SW19 in July, enjoying holidays in Spain with friends and France, the country of his birth, before returning to the practice courts.

Since rocketing up the rankings with his Wimbledon run, attention has been paid to managing his new reality of tour-level tournaments and Grand Slam main draw berths. Modestly, life has changed ‘a little bit’.

‘Because of the tournaments I’m playing, because of the people I’m around, the players I’m around,’ he conceded. ‘But I’m trying not to change my way of approaching business.’

‘I feel like I’m in the prime of my career,’ he added. ‘I feel good in my body. I’m playing the best tournaments in the world.’

Fery’s impact on his British cohort, inspired by the rapid change of circumstance his Wimbledon wins afforded him, is already filtering through in New York. After Toby Samuel booked his spot in the second round on Sunday, he was joined by fellow qualifiers Harriet Dart and Jacob Fearnley.

Dart came through a gutsy three-set win against home favourite Peyton Stearns, with her famous coach, 2013 Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli watching from the stands. The world No131 revealed that she had been almost ‘surprised’ to have beaten Stearns, who ranked 76 places on the heels of their 3-6, 6-3, 6-2 battle.

Fearnley endured a rain-delayed odyssey against rising Spanish starlet Martin Landaluce, with weather again stopping him at match point in the fifth set. Knuckling down when play restarted, he swept the world No65 4-6, 6-2, 4-6, 7-5, 6-3.

Harry Wendelken, who also qualified to play in the Big Apple, plays Luciano Darderi on Monday, with Jan Choinski and Francesca Jones, the final first-round British prospects, in action on Tuesday.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
